releases.summaryHtml: Fixes for test-run exits, migrations, standalone builds and log channels. Shutdown of the HTTP test server, warlock start and per-worker test teardown now stops every running @warlock.js/scheduler scheduler, so a suite whose app starts a scheduler while loading no longer waits out Vitest's 10-second close timeout. warlock migrate releases its lock and closes every data source on every exit path (including Ctrl+C / SIGTERM), bounds the MongoDB connect, prints a heartbeat for long migrations, takes an opt-in --timeout, and names the failing migration and step with recovery advice. build.singleBundle no longer bundles Vite listed under devDependencies, keeps build-time tools out of the bundle, stages aliased native packages under the imported name, stages only reachable native packages and warns about ones it cannot copy. LogChannel.ready resolves after a channel's deferred init, and a channel disposed before init no longer arms its flush timer. No breaking changes. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.39.1 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin.

items.html: A migration that runs long prints still running "<name>", step N of M, <n>s elapsed at 30 s and then every 60 s. Migrations are not aborted by default, so a long index build is never left half-applied.

warlock migrate --timeout <seconds> (or WARLOCK_MIGRATION_TIMEOUT_MS, in milliseconds) opts in to a hard limit per migration. A migration that exceeds it fails with a message naming it, and the command exits 1.

warlock migrate exited without releasing the migration lock or closing the database client, on success, on failure and on Ctrl+C / SIGTERM. Server-side sessions and the lock document were left behind for the server to expire, so a run started soon after another could stall. It now releases the lock and closes every data source before the process exits on every path (exit 130 / 143 on an interrupt), with a bounded wait so shutdown cannot hang.
A failed migration reports which migration (and, on MongoDB, which step) failed, that no ledger row was written, and how to recover.

build.singleBundle no longer bundles Vite when an app lists vite under devDependencies. Only dependencies, optionalDependencies and peerDependencies count as declared by the app, so a dev dependency no longer turns a framework's lazy import() into an inlined package (which had grown dist by about 60 MB and staged the rolldown and lightningcss native addons).

Build-time tools (vite, rolldown, lightningcss, esbuild, oxc-parser, @vitejs/*, @babel/* except @babel/runtime, and their platform packages) are never bundled or staged by singleBundle builds when framework code imports them, even when the app lists them under dependencies. They are kept in one list. A third-party library that imports one at module level is still bundled so it keeps working with no node_modules. The throwing stand-in for oxc-parser applies only when the app does not declare it. Imports from your own source files are unaffected.

A native package installed under an npm alias ("node-pty": "npm:@lydell/node-pty") is staged in dist/node_modules under the name that is imported (node-pty), not under the real package name, so the import resolves from dist/.
Native packages are staged only when the finished bundle still imports them.
The build prints a warning naming a native package it could not copy because its os / cpu / libc exclude the build machine, instead of skipping it silently.

The HTTP test server's shutdown now stops every @warlock.js/scheduler scheduler that is still running. An app that starts a scheduler from a module's boot file (as the scaffolded app does) left a timer armed in the Vitest main process, so a green run ended with close timed out after 10000ms and something prevents N Vite servers from exiting, about ten seconds late. The connectors manager now stops running schedulers, waiting up to app.shutdownTimeout for in-flight jobs, before it tears the connectors down; this also applies to warlock start and other shutdown paths.

MigrationRunner warns while a migration runs long (still running "<name>", step N of M, <n>s elapsed, at 30 s and then every 60 s) and never aborts one by default. A hard limit is opt-in: stepTimeoutMs option, setStepTimeout(ms) / getStepTimeout() or the WARLOCK_MIGRATION_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable. A migration or transactional batch that exceeds it fails with a message naming it. MigrationRunner.releaseActiveLocks() releases the migration lock of a run that is being interrupted. New exports StepTimeoutError and withTimeout.

A MongoDB migration that failed part-way now says which step failed (step 3 of 5: createIndex on "orders"), how many steps were already applied, that no ledger row was written, and that re-running is safe because index creation is idempotent.

MongoDbDriver.connect() is bounded (server selection plus connect timeout, 30 s each by default) and fails with a clear message instead of waiting silently. disconnect() falls back to a forced close when the graceful close stalls for 10 seconds.

LogChannel.ready: a promise that resolves once the channel's deferred init() has finished. Await it before relying on the channel being set up, for example before removing its storage directory in a test.

A FileLog / JSONFileLog disposed before its deferred init() ran still created its directory and armed the 5-second flush interval afterwards, which kept the process alive and could fail with ENOENT when the directory had been removed. A disposed channel now skips init(), including when dispose() lands while init() is creating the directory.

A started scheduler is now listed in a process-wide registry until it stops, so the host (@warlock.js/core) can stop it on shutdown. Previously an application that never called shutdown() kept the process alive through the scheduler's tick timer.
shutdown() no longer leaves its timeout timer armed when the running jobs finish first.

releases.summaryHtml: Standalone builds, release notes in every install and typed-model fixes. build.singleBundle now works with web pages: the server is one dist/app.js that runs with no node_modules, native addons are staged automatically, optional integrations are detected, build-time tools are left out and React runs its production build. webConnector({ build: { chunks, precompress } }) controls the client output (split, merged or single chunks, with or without .br/.gz copies), with a desktop and offline recipe. The release summaries now ship inside @warlock.js/core, read by warlock release-notes (--from, --list, --json) and pointed to by warlock upgrade and warlock update. Typed models accept their system columns (id, timestamps, soft delete) and set() reports value mismatches clearly. Config files no longer walk the app graph at boot, onPageError() registers the error-report hook at runtime, and warlock doctor warns when config imports app code. Browser requests that core refuses on a page host render the site page. New apps and warlock upgrade --check install on npm 10.9. No breaking changes. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.39.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin.

items.html: warlock doctor check config-app-imports: warns when a file under src/config imports (statically or with import()) anything under src/app, naming the file and the import. Type-only imports are not reported.
Route option handlesRefusals and the refusalStatusOf(request) helper. A GET route marked handlesRefusals answers core-level refusals for requests that accept HTML.

warlock release-notes prints the family release summaries that now ship inside the package (releases/<version>-summary.md, 5.30.0 onward). With no arguments it prints the installed version's summary; --from <version> (optionally --to <version>) prints every release after it, oldest first, led by a combined list of breaking changes; --version <v> prints one release; --list lists the versions with dates; --json prints { versions: [{ version, date, breaking, markdown }] }. It reads files only, so it needs no network and no booted app. A version the package does not ship is reported with its GitHub release URL.

warlock upgrade, warlock upgrade --check and warlock update end with What's new: npx warlock release-notes --from <old>, and the AGENTS.md section that warlock agents-md generates names the installed version and the command.
The update-packages, deploy-release and upgrade-from-5-29 skills tell agents to run npx warlock release-notes --from <current> before upgrading.
--version and -v print the Warlock version only when no command is given, so a command can take its own --version option.

The production bundle defines globalThis.__WARLOCK_PRODUCTION_BUNDLE__ as true, so framework branches that only the development server or the build can reach are removed from it together with the modules they import. A build.define entry of the same name overrides it.

WL9024 applies to any integration spec (any *.spec.ts or *.test.ts that is not *.unit.*, or anything under tests/), and its fix text now says to rename the file to <name>.unit.spec.ts outside tests/ (it still said *.test.ts to *.spec.ts). This corrects the 5.38.0 note below.

warlock upgrade --check installs in the scratch copy with npx -y npm@11.6.2 when the npm on PATH is older (npm 10.9 crashes on the family's lockfile with Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut'), which skipped every later step); --from is inferred from the installed @warlock.js/core.

Loading config files walked every module the config reached. loadConfigFiles registered each config file together with its whole transitive import graph (dynamic import() included), file by file, in every process that loads config. A config such as src/config/web.ts whose errors.report imported an application service made each test worker spend minutes in setup; the walk grew with the size of the application (about 480 seconds for a 3,000-module graph, measured). Config files are now registered with their direct import edges only; the dev server still builds the full graph from its own scan.

A request core refuses before routing answered raw JSON to a browser: a dot-segment or path-traversal path on the public mount (/public/../x, 403) and a malformed URL (400). When the app has a route marked handlesRefusals (the web package's page catch-all), a GET or HEAD request that accepts text/html is handed to it; other requests keep the JSON answer.

build.singleBundle now builds an app that uses @warlock.js/web: the server pages and routes are inlined into dist/app.js, and node dist/app.js starts from a copy of dist/ with no node_modules above it.

Optional integrations need no hand-written external list. In a singleBundle build, a lazy import() or require() of an optional peer (or optional dependency) that a framework package lists and the app does not declare stays a lazy runtime import that never runs, and the build report names it. An import the app itself makes, or a package the app declares, is still bundled or fails the build.

Native addons are handled automatically in a singleBundle build. A package with a .node binary (or a napi loader whose platform package holds one) stays external and is copied into dist/node_modules/<package> with only what it needs to load: its JavaScript, binaries and data files, the dependencies it loads and the platform packages that match this machine. The build report names each one.
warlock build prints the number of files and the total size of dist/ when it finishes.

A singleBundle build settles process.env.NODE_ENV to "production" inside react, react-dom and scheduler only, so React's development build is dropped from the bundle. A process.env.NODE_ENV entry in build.define turns this off. Other reads of NODE_ENV are untouched.

In a singleBundle build the native parser oxc-parser, imported by framework code that only the build, check and scan commands call, is replaced by a module that throws if it is ever called. The build names it, and dist/node_modules is created only for native packages the app itself uses.
warlock build in a source checkout runs the route-registration child from its TypeScript source through the CLI loader when the compiled child is absent, instead of failing.

A singleBundle build failed on react-dom/server.node: the native-addon plugin took any import specifier ending in .node for a compiled addon. It now treats only a path that resolves to a real .node file as one.

onPageError(hook), exported from @warlock.js/web/connector: registers a server error-report hook at runtime, from a module's main.ts. It receives the same (error, context) as web.errors.report, runs through the same bounded fire-and-forget queue next to it, and returns a function that removes it. Use it instead of importing application code into src/config/web.ts. Exports the PageErrorHook, PageErrorInfo and PageErrorKind types.

A core-level refusal on a page host answered raw JSON in a browser: /public/../x (403, dot-segment guard) and a malformed URL (400). A GET or HEAD request that names text/html in Accept now renders the site's forbidden.page.tsx for 401 and 403, otherwise error.page.tsx, then the framework fallback page, with the refused status. In multi-site mode the site is chosen by host as for any page. API clients and other requests keep the JSON answer.

Connector build options webConnector({ build: { chunks, precompress } }). chunks is "split" (the default: a React vendor chunk, the entry, a lazy chunk per page and shared chunks), "merged" (the same lazy page loading with small shared chunks packed together by size, far fewer files) or "single" (one JavaScript entry and one stylesheet, dynamic imports inlined; single-site apps only). precompress: false skips the .br and .gz copies of every client asset (default true). Final-bytes chunk names, dedupe, the integrity check, preload lists and payload budgets work in every mode. build.singleBundle in core does not change them; the desktop and offline app recipe sets both.
Exports from @warlock.js/web/vite: ClientChunkMode, resolveClientChunkMode and clientCodeSplitting; buildHydrationClient takes chunks.

A production server built with singleBundle carried Vite and the development server inside app.js, through the connector's build contribution and its development-server branches. The page scanner and the Babel parser came in the same way, through the development page installer and the server barrel the production installer loaded. All of them are left out of the production bundle, and the server never loads Vite.

A build copied away from its project could not find its client bundle: the page manifest stored dist/client relative to the working directory. When a client folder sits next to the running bundle it is used, so node app.js works from any working directory in a copy of dist/.

get() and set() on a model declared with a schema type accept Cascade's system columns without declaring them: id (number), _id, created_at / updated_at (Date), deleted_at (Date | null) and their camelCase spellings. A column the schema declares keeps its own type, so a renamed timestamp or a string id goes in the schema. New ModelSystemColumns and ModelColumns types.
set(key, value) with a wrong value type now reports the value mismatch instead of a misleading error about dot paths. A column named at runtime is set with a key typed K extends ModelKey<Schema>.

npm install in a fresh scaffold no longer crashes on npm 10.9 (the npm bundled with Node 22) with Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut'): the template pins Vitest 5.0.5, because the Vitest releases before it trip that npm bug on their own. The edgesOut hint stays as a last resort.

releases.summaryHtml: Persistent request log, faster test runtimes, stable chunk names and typed models. http.logging.requests writes one redacted record per request, read by devtools (history, copy as curl), warlock logs and the MCP request_log tool, and every 5xx is logged once as request.<phase>. New apps run tests with worker lifetime and per-file resets, *.unit.spec.ts files run without booting the app, the HTTP test server closes the web connector's Vite servers, and tests.profileSetup prints a per-phase boot profile. Production chunks are named after their final bytes, identical chunks are merged, builds check integrity against the previous build and enforce payload budgets. Seal keeps optional enums and literals nullable in openai-strict and names unlabelled fields in words; AI tools get per-provider schema lint, a tool-use contract, eval scorers and agent traces in devtools. Page routes render a per-site forbidden.page.tsx instead of JSON for 401/403, warlock upgrade --check rehearses upgrades, warlock doctor renders each site, typed capabilities and inspect --section wiring show auto-loaded wiring, and *.client.ts(x) is an enforced client-only boundary. Breaking: typed models type get() and set() from their schema. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.38.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin.

items.html: Test file convention: *.unit.spec.ts and *.unit.test.ts run in the Vitest unit project (no setup files, no app boot, threads pool); every other *.spec.ts and *.test.ts, and anything under tests/, runs in the integration project. guardUnitProject() checks the .unit. files, and WL9024 now flags any integration spec that never touches the app and suggests renaming it to <name>.unit.spec.ts. Existing apps keep their own globs; the 5.38 upgrade note and the test-runtime-worker-lifetime step list how to adopt the convention.

Validation messages name a field without a translated label in words: max_dumbbell_kg reads "Max dumbbell kg" and firstName reads "First name" instead of the raw key. Labels under attributes.<field> still win, and validation.attributes.<field> is read too when validation.attributeGroup is not set. Only the validated field and sibling fields a rule refers to are turned into words. validation.humanizeAttributes: false keeps the raw key.
warlock doctor check validation-labels (WL4002), off by default: with validation.warnMissingLabels: true it lists request-schema fields that have no label in a locale of app.localeCodes.

warlock check rule WL9021 (warning): a Cascade column read or written as a model property (user.email). It recognises instances from new User(), the single-record finders (find, first, create, ...), a User annotation and this inside a model class, and compares the name with the keys of the model's static schema when they can be read statically. warlock check --fix rewrites reads to model.get("column") and plain model.column = value; statements to model.set("column", value).

Every 5xx the HTTP layer answers writes one error-level log record (module: "http", action: "request.<phase>"), once per request, in the same shape as the page-failure record of @warlock.js/web: name, message, stack, phase (csrf, middleware, validation or handler), file (the routes file), routeName, routePath, handler, middleware (the middleware that threw), method, pathname (no query string), requestId and statusCode. It covers throws from route middleware, request validation and controllers, and a 5xx a handler returned without throwing; a returned 503 is treated as an intentional answer and not logged. A 4xx is never logged as an error. With no log channel configured the failure still goes to console.error.
In development the JSON error body of a thrown error and of the opaque 500 includes requestId. Production bodies are unchanged.

Persistent request log, http.logging.requests: one redacted JSON record per request, written after the response is sent through buffered logger channels. A record holds the id and trace id, time, method, URL (credential query values masked), route name and pattern, params, query, headers, body, session: { userId, userType }, IP, status, duration, response size (and headers and body when include.response is on), phases, the log entries emitted during the request, a query summary (count, slowest query, N+1 findings) and, for a 5xx or a request that threw, the error with its stack, phase, page file and site. RequestLogRecord, listRequestLogs(), getRequestLog(), requestLogToCurl() and compileRequestLogFilter() are exported.

http.logging.requests options: enabled (default on in development, off elsewhere), channels (logger channel names or instances; default a daily JSON-lines file storage/logs/requests/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl), only ("all", "errors", "slow"; default "all" in development and "errors" elsewhere), slowMs, sampleRate (errors are always kept when only includes them), include (headers, body, query, params, session, response, stack, logs, queries, phases), maxBodyBytes (default 16 KB, a larger body ends with a truncation marker) and retention: { maxDays, maxSizeMb } for the default file channel, which prunes on boot and when a new day's file starts.

Outside development the request log records request headers through an allowlist, and leaves the request and response bodies out unless include.body / include.response is set. The logger's redaction, http.logging.private URL rules and a route's logging: { body: false, query: false } apply to every record, and uploaded files are recorded as { file, mimeType } only.
warlock logs requests [--status 5xx|404] [--route name] [--since 1h] [--limit n] [--json] lists persisted requests and warlock logs request <id> [--json] prints one in full. Neither boots the app.
MCP tool request_log (read-only): lists persisted requests with status, route, method, since, q and limit filters, or returns one full record by id.
Skill request-log.

warlock add test generates the new layout: the unit project includes src/**/*.unit.{spec,test}.ts, and integration includes src/**/*.{spec,test}.ts, src//tests//*.{test,spec}.ts and tests/**/*.{test,spec}.ts, excluding *.unit.*. An existing vite.config.ts is never overwritten.

The three separate error-level entries for a 5xx (request-error, model-write-validation-error and unhandled-request-error) are replaced by the single record above. The per-request http.log line is unchanged.

setupTest({ lifetime: "file" }) opts one file out of a worker-scoped runtime (tests.lifetime: "worker"). The worker's shared runtime is shut down, the file boots a fresh one that its own teardownTest() closes, and the next file returns to the worker lifetime. Use it for a spec that changes global configuration the per-file reset does not undo.

A worker-scoped runtime now resets more between files, in addition to the database and the fakes: test HTTP servers left open are closed, the request context is cleared, the route table returns to the snapshot taken after the app booted (routes a file registered by hand are removed, the app's own stay), and a real in-memory cache driver is flushed. router.captureBootSnapshot() and router.restoreBootSnapshot() are the router side of it.

Per-phase boot profile. With tests.profileSetup: true or WARLOCK_TEST_PROFILE=1, each file's profile also carries one connector.<name> entry per connector (boot() plus start()) and appModules, startHttpTestServer() prints and publishes its own phases, and TestSetupReporter prints the phases (config, translations, connectors, fakes, routes, reset, teardown), each connector, the HTTP test server's boot and the slowest files in the run summary. WARLOCK_TEST_PROFILE_JSON=<path> or new TestSetupReporter({ json, slowest }) also writes the profile as JSON. connectorsManager.observeTimings() exposes the connector timings.

guardUnitProject() in @warlock.js/core/vite: a plugin for the Vitest unit project that fails a spec importing a connector, connectorsManager, bootstrap or a test-server helper, or calling setupTest() without { mode: "unit" }, with a message naming the import and pointing to the integration project. setupTest() outside unit mode also throws when WARLOCK_TEST_PROJECT=unit.
warlock check reports WL9024 (a warning) for an integration spec (*.test.ts, or a spec under tests/) that imports nothing needing the app, with the hint to move it to the unit project.

Upgrade codemod test-runtime-worker-lifetime lists where an existing app can opt in to the worker lifetime (src/config/tests.ts without a lifetime) and a unit project without guardUnitProject(). It edits nothing; existing apps keep their test configuration. The 5.38 upgrade note says the same.

warlock add test generates the worker lifetime as the default: src/config/tests.ts sets lifetime: "worker" and resetDatabase: true unless WARLOCK_TEST_LIFETIME=file, the integration project has isolate: false from the same variable, and the unit project runs in threads with guardUnitProject(). Existing files are never overwritten.

Auto-loaded utils/locales.ts is deprecated. The development and production-build warning now names every legacy file, and WL9101 already lists them in warlock doctor. Removal is planned for v6, not this release; move to utils/locales.json with warlock doctor --fix.
The starter template (create-warlock) ships JSON dictionaries (app/auth/utils/locales.json, app/shared/utils/locales/*.json) instead of utils/locales.ts.

The console.error fallback for an unhandled request error, used when no log channel is configured, ignores passive channels (see LogChannel.passive in @warlock.js/logger), so the request log's log collector never silences it.
warlock ai no longer marks --model as required in its option list; warlock ai measure still requires it and reports a missing value.

Loading warlock.config.ts keeps @warlock.js/* imports external even when the project's tsconfig paths maps them to local source (a monorepo checkout). The config bundle used to inline a second copy of core and the web connector, whose container never held the application's HTTP server.
The HTTP test server (startHttpTestServer()) registers the connectors warlock.config.ts declares, as warlock dev does. The web connector was never started under it, so a page request answered 404.

A test run that booted the web connector no longer ends with something prevents 2 Vite servers from exiting and close timed out after 10000ms. stopHttpTestServer() and the worker teardown shut the web connector down even when it had booted but not started, closing Vite, its HMR websocket and its file watchers, and teardown names any connector still active afterwards.

The 5.36 upgrade note and the testing docs and skills now say that Vitest 5's clearMocks: true default also clears calls a module made when it was imported (a scheduler registering jobs from a main.ts), before the first test runs. Import the module inside the test, or set clearMocks: false.

warlock upgrade --check: rehearses an upgrade on a scratch copy of the app and never writes the real project. The project (without node_modules, .git and storage) is copied to a temporary directory, the upgrade (package.json and codemods) is applied there, dependencies are installed there with the app's package manager, and typings, typecheck, warlock doctor and the unit Vitest project run against the result. The report lists the breaking changes that hit the app and the outcome of each step. Every child process runs one at a time, at low priority, with a heap cap (--memory-mb, default 4096) and a time limit (--timeout-minutes, default 20); --skip-install applies the upgrade to the copy and stops there, and --keep leaves the copy on disk. Exit code 1 when a step failed.

warlock doctor check sites: in an app with web.sites, renders the root page of every site with fixed hostnames through the development page pipeline, in this process with no port, and fails (WL5005) with the status, the phase and the page file of any 5xx.

Capabilities: defineCapability<T>(name, { description, required }), provideCapability(capability, implementation), useCapability(capability), hasCapability(capability) and listCapabilities() give a module-cycle-breaking slot a typed, discoverable home. useCapability throws WL2008 when nothing provided it. warlock doctor warns (WL2008) when a required capability has no provider after boot (check capabilities).

warlock inspect --section wiring and the MCP tool inspect_wiring: every auto-loaded file (config, locales, events, main.ts, routes.ts, workers) with its module and boot load order, followed by every capability slot with its provider and consumers. The section is part of the inspect report JSON Schema.
New skill use-capabilities.

warlock agents-md lists the skill of a package that ships a single skills/SKILL.md (for example the AI provider packages and @warlock.js/sitemap). Its slug is the front-matter name, else the package name.

Package manager detection no longer lets a stale pnpm-workspace.yaml and pnpm-lock.yaml win over the lockfile actually in use. The order is now the packageManager field; then the manager that installed node_modules (.package-lock.json for npm, .pnpm or .modules.yaml for pnpm, .yarn-state.yml or .yarn-integrity for yarn, .bun for Bun); then the lockfile that lists every dependency of package.json, else bun.lock, else the most recently written one; a pnpm-workspace.yaml counts only when there is no lockfile at all. warlock update always prints which manager it chose and why.

warlock check reports WL9022 when server-only code (controllers, services, repositories, models, connectors, routes.ts, main.ts, worker.ts, events/ and *.server.* files) imports a *.client.ts(x) module, directly or through other files. The message names the import chain, and a type-only import is not reported.

warlock check reports WL9105 when a translation key of a module dictionary is missing a configured locale. The configured locales are localeCodes in src/config/app.ts, or localeCodes in .warlock-check.json, which wins; the rule is skipped when neither names any.
Opt-in WL9023 finds hand-maintained index.ts barrels in app modules (an index.ts that only re-exports). It is off until .warlock-check.json sets rules.WL9023 to "warning" or "error".

Per-feature locale files: src/app/<module>/utils/locales/<feature>.json is merged with the module's utils/locales.json in development, in the production build and in test workers, under the module's namespace unless the file names its own $group. A key may live in one file only. Web's per-page translation tables are built from the same registry, so they see the merged dictionary.

generate: { barrels: false } in warlock.config.ts makes warlock generate, warlock make and warlock add access write no index.ts barrel (for models) and import the model file itself in the files they generate. The default stays true.

warlock doctor --fix converts a legacy utils/locales.ts into utils/locales/legacy.json when the module already has a locales.json, as long as no key appears in both; it still writes locales.json when there is none.

warlock ai tools --tools <module> lists each tool's estimated tokens per call and its per-provider schema findings (OpenAI strict, Anthropic, Google); --targets, --warn-above, --fail (exit 1 on an error-level finding) and --json.

warlock ai trace [runId] reads the agent traces held by the running dev server: a run list, or one run turn by turn (system prompt hash, tools offered, calls, refusals, retries, usage, cost); --diff <otherRunId> compares the prompt and tool definitions of two runs; --url, --devtools-path and --json. Both need @warlock.js/ai 5.38.0 or newer.

warlock build measures build.budgets.payload for the sections the build knows: each page's pruned translations and its browser route table, both upper bounds. A page whose measured sections exceed its limit fails the build with mode: "error" and prints a warning with mode: "warn"; the message gives the per-section breakdown and says which sections (page, layout, app and session data, other) are only measured at runtime. The runtime check is unchanged and still never fails a request.

Client build integrity: every build writes client/.vite/warlock-integrity.json (a digest per file in client/assets). The next warlock build reads the previous record before it starts and fails, naming each file, when a file name now maps to different bytes. The new web build option previousBuild points the comparison at another build's record or output directory (for example the deployed release). New exports from @warlock.js/web/vite: ChunkIntegrityError, CHUNK_INTEGRITY_FILE, readChunkIntegrity and the ChunkIntegrityRecord and ChunkIntegrityConflict types; buildHydrationClient takes previousIntegrity.

Two request tracing phases through core's TracingHooks.onPhase: translations (route, locale, mode) around binding the page's translation snapshot, and named-api-routes (route) around resolving the document's route table.

*.client.ts(x) is now an enforced client-only boundary. Pages, layouts and components may import it, and it renders on the server unless the component is wrapped in <ClientOnly>; server-only code (loaders in setup files, controllers, services, repositories, models, routes, connectors and *.server.ts files) may not import it. In development SSR such an import is an error naming the import chain instead of a warning. warlock check reports the same import as WL9022.

The console.error fallback for a page failure, used when no log channel is configured, ignores passive channels (for example the collector behind Core's request log), so the failure still reaches the terminal.

apiHref() and useSubmitForm({ route }) called while a page renders on the server found no route table when the page code and the renderer were separate copies of the framework module (the development SSR graph, with an application alias for @warlock.js/web). The renderer now publishes the document's table where every copy reads it.

In development, the document's browser route table was empty when the renderer ran through Vite SSR as a separate copy of @warlock.js/core (an HTTP test server or dev server with an application alias), so apiHref() found no route. The page handlers now carry the real router registry to the renderer, which reads the table from it.

A multi-site app in development answered every site hostname with Vite's "Blocked request. This host is not allowed" (403). The dev server now allows the hostnames listed in web.sites, and any host when a site is dynamic.

Production client chunks are named after their final bytes. The bundler hashed a chunk before the import specifiers inside it were rewritten, so two builds that differed only in the name of an imported chunk emitted the same file name for different bytes, and two byte-identical chunks could keep different names. After the bundle is written, chunks are renamed in dependency order from the hash of their final code (chunks that import each other are named together), byte-identical non-entry chunks are merged into one file (the budget report keeps the modules of every merged chunk), and the client manifest, the module preload lists, the budget report and the precompressed .br and .gz files all use the final names.

Production pages no longer walk the whole named route registry on every request. A page's browser route table is resolved once per site and viewer kind and reused; development still resolves it per request, because its registry and files change. A web.namedApiRoutes filter function is therefore called once per route, site and viewer kind in production.
A render that built its hydration payload more than once (the document context, the final payload, a data request) pruned the global translation registry each time; it is now pruned once per request.

forbidden.page.tsx (with an optional forbidden.setup.ts): the application's page for a refused request. A 401 or 403 on a page route renders it with that status. It declares no config.route, a second copy fails the build (one per site in multi-site mode, at $sites/<name>/forbidden.page.tsx), and it receives the same { error, status } props as error.page.tsx, plus debug outside production. A request renders the site's (or the app's) forbidden page, then its error.page.tsx with the 401/403 status, then the framework default. The page manifest gains forbiddenPage (and a forbiddenPage entry per site), the client registry projects it as ForbiddenPage, and hydration picks it by the same rule, so the browser hydrates the page the server rendered. Discovery exports DiscoveredForbiddenPage, isForbiddenPageFile and DuplicateForbiddenPageError.

The framework's own fallback page now shows the request id and a "Back to home" link, and a 401/403 gets its own plain, accessible "You don't have access to this page." message. Outside production the development details panel still follows it.

requireUser({ userType }) and requireUser({ when }) answered a failed check with a raw JSON body ({"error":"Forbidden"}) on a page route. The middleware form now throws ForbiddenError (and UnAuthorizedError for a guest with no sign-in page or a bearer client), so a page route renders the forbidden page instead. A guest with auth.pageAuth.loginPath is still redirected to sign in. To refuse a page request from your own middleware, throw a Core ForbiddenError; response.forbidden() still writes its own JSON reply.
In development, hydrating an error page failed with a malformed-payload error because the payload check rejected the debug details the server sends outside production. The check now accepts debug.
A route-translations lookup for a failure rendered by the error or forbidden page now covers both pages' keys.

WebConnector.shutdown() closes the Vite dev server, its HMR websocket and its file watchers whenever Vite was created, not only after start() completed. A boot that failed after creating Vite, or a shutdown between boot() and start(), used to leave Vite running and keep a test or dev process from exiting. A failure to close one part no longer skips the others, and the first failure is reported afterwards.

The client build enforces a module boundary: browser code may import from app/<module>/... only browser-safe files, which are *.client.ts(x), schema files (*.schema.ts or a schema/ folder), type files (*.types.ts, *.d.ts or a types/ folder), the module's web/ folder and non-code files. Any other file (a controller, service, repository, model, route file or plain helper) fails the build with the import chain. A type-only import is erased and always allowed. web.moduleBoundary sets "warn" (default: report and continue, so an existing app upgrades without a broken build), "error" (fail the build) or "off", in development and in warlock build.

Development SSR warns once per *.client.* module that reads window, document, navigator, localStorage or another browser global while it is being imported (outside a function or a typeof guard), naming the file and line.

Model.get() and Model.set() are typed from the model's schema type. get("publishedAt") is Date | null, a column with a .default() is never undefined, get(key, default) drops null and undefined, and set(key, value) rejects a value of the wrong type. Dot paths ("profile.city") stay loosely typed (any, or the type argument you pass) so large schemas do not slow the compiler. A model declared without a schema type keeps loose access.
ModelData<typeof schema> (the schema's output type, casts applied), ModelDataSnapshot<T>, ModelKey, ModelValue and ModelPath types.
model.toDataSnapshot(): a typed, read-only copy of the model's data without its hidden columns, for resources and presenters that want exact types.

Model.requestSchema() returns the model schema without the fields marked .internal(), so a server-set field is declared once and request schemas derived from the model omit it. Model.create() still accepts those fields.
In development, reading a schema column as a property (model.title) logs one warning per model and column that names model.get("title"). Nothing is installed when NODE_ENV is production.

BREAKING For a model declared with a schema type, get() and set() with a top-level column name that is not in the schema are now type errors. Add the column to the schema, use a dot path, or declare the model without a schema type to keep loose access.
A model declared with a schema type is assignable to the loose Model and ChildModel again, so helpers, migrations and this-typed statics accept typed models unchanged.

The web template ships src/web/forbidden.page.tsx and forbidden.setup.ts (styled by forbidden.css, imported from app.css): the page a 401/403 on a page route renders instead of raw JSON. The template README and the web-code-standards skill describe it.

The starter ships src/config/web.ts with moduleBoundary: "error", so browser code importing a server-only module file fails the client build in new apps (the framework default for existing apps is "warn").
The generated testing guidance and code standards use the *.unit.spec.ts / *.unit.test.ts convention for unit specs (the test feature's unit and integration Vitest projects pick files by that infix).

The starter boots the test framework once per Vitest worker: src/config/tests.ts sets lifetime: "worker" and resetDatabase: true (WARLOCK_TEST_LIFETIME=file switches back), and src/config/database.ts (and the PostgreSQL variant) uses one database per Vitest worker, <DB_NAME>_test_<worker id>. With --features=test the generated unit project fails a spec that imports a connector or boots the app, and the integration project runs with isolate: false. The PostgreSQL variant needs those databases created and migrated first.
The template's testing-strategy skill describes the per-file reset, the setupTest({ lifetime: "file" }) opt-out, the unit-project guard, WL9024, the boot profile and Vitest 5's clearMocks default.

The starter app keeps translations in JSON: app/auth/utils/locales.json and app/shared/utils/locales/{validation,http,attributes}.json replace the two utils/locales.ts files, and docs/new-module.md describes locales.json and locales/<feature>.json.

The template's module-boundaries, code-standards and web-code-standards skills describe small exported types co-located in *.service.ts, optional barrels (and the opt-in WL9023 lint), the browser-safe surface of an app module and the *.client.ts(x) boundary.

The Requests panel and GET /__warlock/api/requests also read core's persistent request log (storage/logs/requests/*.jsonl), so request history survives a restart and the 200-request ring buffer. Live and persisted requests are merged without duplicates by request id; requests read only from disk are marked persisted.

Request filters: the list API takes status (404 or a class such as 5xx), route, method, since, until, q (text in the URL or id) and limit, answering 400 for a bad value; the dashboard has search, status and method filters.

A saved request opens with its error (message, stack, phase, page file, site), the redacted request and response, the log entries and the query summary with N+1 findings. GET /__warlock/api/requests/:id carries the full record as record.
Copy as curl: GET /__warlock/api/requests/:id/curl and a button in the request detail. Values the log redacted stay [REDACTED].

Agents tab at /__warlock for the per-turn agent traces @warlock.js/ai records in development: system prompt, tools offered with schema hashes and token estimates, tool calls with results and refusals, retries and re-prompts, usage and cost, and a comparison with the previous run of the same agent. It needs no Panoptic.

GET /__warlock/api/ai/agent-runs (optionally ?requestId=) and GET /__warlock/api/ai/agent-runs/:id, plus agent-trace events on the stream, behind the existing development and loopback guard. Runs started during an HTTP request link to it. Types DevtoolsAgentRun and DevtoolsAgentTraceEvent.
humanizeAttribute(key) turns a field key into words (max_dumbbell_kg becomes "Max dumbbell kg").
ObjectValidator#partial() keeps its types: the named keys (all keys when none are named) become optional in the inferred shape.

toJsonSchema("openai-strict") keeps an optional v.enum(), v.literal(), in() list or union nullable: null is added to an enum, a const becomes anyOf: [{ const }, { type: "null" }], anyOf/oneOf gain one { type: "null" } branch, and allOf/$ref schemas are wrapped in anyOf. Before, such fields were listed in required with no way to send null.

.nullable() on an enum, a literal, a scalar or a union no longer produces a type of [undefined, "null"] for draft-2020-12; the same shapes as above are used, and openapi-3.0 adds null to the enum next to nullable: true. A nullable single literal now emits anyOf: [{ const }, { type: "null" }] instead of a bare const.

.internal() marks a field as set by the server. It validates and infers like any other field; ObjectValidator#withoutInternal() returns the schema without those fields (type included) for request validation, and internalKeys() lists them. BaseValidator#isServerSet() reads the mark.
translateAttribute passed to v.validate(schema, data, options) now translates the :input placeholder too; before, only the global config's translator was used for attribute labels.

ai.tool() checks its JSON Schema against OpenAI strict, Anthropic and Google when the tool is defined and, in development only, logs one warning per tool definition: optional fields sent as required and nullable, properties missing from required, objects without additionalProperties: false, unsupported keywords (allOf, oneOf, not, conditionals, patternProperties, ...), non-object roots, invalid names, oversized descriptions and heavy definitions. lint: false or lint: { targets, warnAboveTokens, ... } on a tool and ai.config({ toolLint }) tune or silence it.

describeToolSchema(tool, options?) and describeToolSchemas(tools, options?) (also ai.tools.describe / ai.tools.describeAll) return the findings, a schema hash and an estimated token cost per definition; formatToolSchemaReports() prints them. The token figure is an estimate (charsPerToken, default 4); ai.tools.measure stays the exact native count.

Opt-in tool-use contract on agents. actWhenAsked: { intents, requiredTools } re-prompts once when an action request is answered without a required tool call. onToolRefusal: "retry-once-with-hint" (or { retries, hint, isRefusal }) sends one retry prompt with the refusal reason when the model gives up after a tool refused a call. backstops: [{ phase, detect(turn), run(context) }] run deterministic checks before the first model call or after a final answer, and may return a prompt to send the model. Agents without these options behave exactly as before.

Eval scorers ai.eval.requiredToolCalled({ tools, intents?, require? }) ("required tool not called") and ai.eval.changeClaimedWithoutToolCall({ tools?, claims? }) ("change claimed without a tool call").

Agent traces. Each agent run records a per-turn trace: system prompt (hash, and text in development), tools offered with schema hashes and token estimates, tool calls, results, refusals, tool-use contract actions, token usage and cost. On in development, off under test and in production; trace: true | false | { enabled, text, redact, maxStringLength, store } per agent (an options object records in development only unless enabled: true). Traces are redacted with the logger's secret-key rules and registered credentials, and kept in the shared in-memory agentTraces store (get, list, subscribe, clear; createAgentTraceStore() for another). diffAgentTraces(a, b) reports whether two runs sent the same system prompt and tool definitions; formatAgentTrace(trace) renders one as text.

LogChannel.passive: a channel that only observes entries (keeps them in memory, derives data from them) and persists nothing sets it to true. Code that falls back to the terminal "when no log channel is configured" ignores passive channels, so adding an observer never silences that fallback.

releases.summaryHtml: Multi-site development fix, page error logging and npm family upgrades. Multi-site pages no longer answer 500 in development and under the HTTP test server (the route table is read from Core's router; web.namedApiRoutes: false skips it). Every 5xx page failure logs one error record with the message, mapped stack, phase, page file, route, site and request id, and the development error page shows the same details. warlock update on npm removes the family's lock entries and re-resolves them in one install (npm 11.6.2 or newer), WL8010 reports mixed family versions, and warlock upgrade no longer downgrades newer packages and names the package manager the project uses. Vitest 5 no longer warns about a repeated lowerStage3Decorators(), worker lifetime supports HTTP and database suites (tests.resetDatabase, workerDatabaseName()), HMR attaches through Vite 8's server.ws, and the client-bundle check no longer reports the app's index.html. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.37.1 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin.

items.html: tests.resetDatabase (true or { connection, except, only }): with tests.lifetime: "worker", truncates every table or collection of the data source before each file, keeping the migrations ledger and system collections, then runs tests.resetBetweenFiles. resetTestDatabase(), workerDatabaseName(base) and testWorkerId() are exported from @warlock.js/core/tests so each Vitest worker can use a database of its own.
A worker-lifetime runtime closes the createTestHttpServer() servers a file left open before the next file starts, so their routes and ports do not leak across files.

The setup profile reports body, the time between setup finishing and teardown starting. When a file-lifetime run of at least four files spends half or more of its time in setup, the worker summary and TestSetupReporter print a line recommending tests.lifetime: "worker".

warlock add test generates src/config/tests.ts. WARLOCK_TEST_LIFETIME=worker turns on worker lifetime and resetDatabase, and the generated integration project sets isolate: false from the same variable.
Upgrade codemod vitest-inline-project-plugins lists a lowerStage3Decorators() call repeated inside a Vitest config that declares projects.

The exact, cyclic pins between @warlock.js/* packages stay (the family is released in lockstep). To get past them, warlock update on npm removes the family's (and vite, vitest, @vitest/* and @vitejs/*) entries from package-lock.json and re-resolves them in one npm install; npm 11.6.2 or newer is required for that step, and WL8010 reports mixed family versions.

Package manager detection with several lockfiles side by side (and no packageManager field or pnpm-workspace.yaml) uses the most recently written one, the lockfile the project installs with, and warlock update says which it chose. bun.lock still wins over the yarn.lock Bun also writes.

Vitest 5 printed The "<project>" project applies the same plugin multiple times: "warlock:lower-stage3-decorators" when a config listed lowerStage3Decorators() in the root and again in an inline project. Instances after the first in a process now carry a numbered plugin name and skip modules that no longer contain a decorator, so the warning is gone and a project that does not inherit the root config still lowers decorators. The docs and skills explain extends for inline projects.

warlock check reports WL8010 when the installed @warlock.js/* packages are on different versions, naming the packages that differ from the newest one and pointing to warlock update. The family stays in lockstep: packages pin each other to the exact same version, so a mixed set is not a valid install.

warlock update for npm projects removes the family's (and Vite's and Vitest's) entries from package-lock.json before the install, so one npm install re-resolves them together, and warns when the npm in use is older than 11.6.2, which npm 10 cannot always do (ERESOLVE, or a crash on the Vitest peer set). It names the install command of the package manager the project uses instead of a generic one.

warlock upgrade no longer moves a @warlock.js/* dependency down: one already newer than --to stays as it is and is listed in the review list. Its install hint names the package manager the project installs with, not the first lockfile found.
@warlock.js/core exports the shared log instance from @warlock.js/logger, so framework packages that depend on core write to the channels the app configured with setLogConfigurations.

Outside production, the error page, an authored ErrorBoundary and the framework fallback are followed by a development panel (data-warlock-dev-error) showing the message, phase, page file, route, site and stack. error.page.tsx receives the same facts as props.debug (PageErrorDetails, new type export). Production responses stay generic and never carry them.
ServerErrorContext (the context of web.errors.report) gains file, site and level; phase takes the values above.

The development server no longer prints server.hmr.protocol/host/port/path/clientPort/timeout/server is deprecated on every boot. The HMR websocket is attached to the app's HTTP server through Vite 8's server.ws.server instead of the deprecated server.hmr.server; hot reload behaves as before.

The client-bundle security check (Gate A) no longer warns could not judge this import for the app's own index.html entry, in either the client or the SSR build. HTML entries and Vite's virtual HTML proxy modules are treated as entries, not imports; a genuinely unresolvable import still warns.

A page that answered 500 left only the Completed Request: … 500 line in the log. Every 5xx page response now writes one error-level logger record (module: "web", action: "page.<phase>") with the error message, the stack, the matched page file, the route pattern, the site key, the request id and the phase: translations, module-load, middleware, session, loader, metadata, render, stream, defer, error-page, request-handler, or unknown for a 5xx nobody reported (for example response.setStatusCode(500) without a throw). With no log channel configured the failure still goes to console.error. Errors that React swallows into an ErrorBoundary or error.page.tsx, errors from onShellError and onError of the stream, and failures while binding route translations or loading the page module are logged too. The same error is logged once however many stages observe it, and a 4xx outcome (not found, redirect, validation, a thrown HttpError below 500) is not logged as an error.

Multi-site apps: pages no longer answer 500 in development and under the HTTP test server with input.router.getNamedApiRoutes is not a function, even with web.namedApiRoutes: false. The browser route table now reads Core's real router registry, never the per-site registration router. With web.namedApiRoutes: false the page's route names are no longer computed at all, and a failure computing the table is logged through the page error log with the new phase named-api-routes instead of a bare 500.
The development stack is mapped back to source files through the dev server (ssrFixStacktrace); in production, run Node with --enable-source-maps.
The template's testing-strategy skill describes WARLOCK_TEST_LIFETIME=worker, resetDatabase and workerDatabaseName() for the generated test setup.

releases.summaryHtml: Field-report fixes: route table controls, safe document-store rollbacks, warlock release and eval variance. Breaking: on MongoDB a plain dropColumn() inside down() is skipped with a warning (pass { destructive: true } to unset; add-only Migration.alter derives a ledger-only rollback), and warlock migrate --rollback/--fresh and the cascade rollback commands print a destructive-operation summary and need confirmation or --yes outside development. web.namedApiRoutes turns the page route table off, limits it with an allowlist or filter, and keeps privatePrefixes out; routes take a sites option for multi-site apps, and guarded routes are left out for known guests. Route inspection, the generated AGENTS.md facts and WL9006 count group guards and markAuthGuard() middleware. warlock release adds candidate, gate, migrations --prove, stage, activate, verify, rollback and prune for application deploys. agent.eval({ repeat }) reports pass counts, Wilson and t intervals, an interval-based regression gate and stable versus flaky failures. Fixes: validation messages never keep an unfilled :placeholder, finished Vitest runs exit on their own (the file logger's flush timer no longer holds the process), pages whose components import CSS work in Node page discovery, and development logs the first hydration mismatch. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.37.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin.

items.html: warlock release <action> [id]: a deploy pipeline for applications, configured by the new release section of warlock.config.ts (ReleaseConfig, ReleaseCheck). candidate freezes a clean commit (--commit, --allow-dirty) into .warlock/releases/<version>-<shortsha>/ with a manifest (version, commit, creation time, Node version, lockfile hash). gate runs an ordered list of named checks (default: typecheck, check, test, build) and stops at the first failure. migrations --prove [--target] snapshots the migration ledger, tables and indexes around a real run of the pending migrations and compares them with the expected set. stage copies the build and what is needed to run it. activate [--preflight] [--dry-run] [--allow-same] checks the staged files, the gate and that the version is strictly greater than the active one, then switches current with an atomic symlink, keeps previous and runs the restart command you configure in release.restart.command; Warlock never calls a process manager itself. verify retries a GET on release.verify.url and compares the reported version and commit with the active release. rollback [--dry-run] switches back and reruns the restart command; it does not roll migrations back. list, status and prune --keep <n> (the only command that deletes releases) complete the family. Every action accepts --json, and a manifest per release plus a release.log record what happened.

sites route option and router.group({ sites }) option: the web.sites keys a multi-site app offers a named API route to in the browser. Absent means shared by every site; a route's own sites replaces its group's. The route snapshot carries sites only on routes that declared it.
The named route snapshot carries guarded: true on a route with an auth guard in its middleware chain (group middleware included), so browser route tables can leave it out for guests.
In development, the first time a validation translation cannot be filled, a warning names its validation.* key.

BREAKING warlock migrate --rollback and warlock migrate --fresh print a destructive-operation summary (collections/tables dropped, fields/columns unset, document/row counts) before running. Outside development they ask for confirmation, and exit with code 1 when there is no terminal. New --yes, -y and --force flags confirm without a prompt.

warlock inspect and the generated AGENTS.md list of "Mutating routes without an auth guard" counted only routes whose guard attached a warlock.auth descriptor. A middleware that declares itself a guard with markAuthGuard(), including one registered once on a router.group, now marks every route inside the group as guarded.

warlock check (WL9006) treats markAuthGuard(fn, false) written inline in a middleware list as not a guard, and recognises a local factory such as const requireAdmin = () => markAuthGuard(fn) used as middleware: [requireAdmin()] in a route or group.

The default validation message translation no longer returns a message with an unfilled :placeholder. When the browser form library is imported on the server, its English validation.* defaults share the translation registry and name the length value :length, where seal uses :minLength and :maxLength, so a v.string().maxLength(5) failure read "This input can not be greater than :length characters". The aliases :length (for minLength and maxLength) and :matchingInput (for match) are now mapped, and a translation that still cannot be filled falls back to seal's own message. App overrides of validation.* keep working.

The dev loader hook answers stylesheet imports (.css, .scss, .sass, .less, .styl) with an empty module, so sitemap discovery works for a page whose component imports a stylesheet instead of failing with ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION.

web.namedApiRoutes controls the route table each page embeds for apiHref() and useSubmitForm({ route }). false embeds nothing: a named-route call then throws, and in development the error names the option (explicit path and method still work). An allowlist of route names (with prefix.* patterns) or a filter function (route, { site, guest }) => boolean narrows the table, and { include, privatePrefixes } combines both. Every form can only remove routes from what the page's client code reaches.

web.namedApiRoutes.privatePrefixes (for example ["/api/admin/", "/api/webhooks/"]) keeps every route under those path prefixes out of every table, for any viewer and any site. Prefixes match whole path segments.

Site scoping: in a multi-site app a page never embeds a route declared for other sites. A route declares its sites with the sites option (see core); a route that declares none is shared by every site.

A route with an auth guard in its middleware chain (group middleware included) is left out of the table for a guest viewer. A viewer is a guest only when web.session is configured and resolves no user; without web.session the viewer is unknown (the app may sign in with tokens in the browser) and guarded routes stay.
Types NamedApiRoutesOption, NamedApiRoutesConfig, NamedApiRoutesInclude, NamedApiRoutesFilter, NamedApiRouteCandidate and NamedApiRouteContext.
Server seam resolveNamedApiRoutes(names, options) takes { config, site, guest }; without options it applies site scoping and guard rules for a guest in single-site mode.
In development, when React reports a hydration mismatch, the client logs the first mismatching node: the element path, the server text and the client text. Production builds are unchanged.

The create-a-page and localize-pages skills and the localization and client/server boundary docs warn that Intl.DisplayNames, localeCompare sorting and similar Intl output can differ between Node and browsers and cause hydration mismatches, and recommend a shared pre-computed table or rendering after hydration.

Migration.alter with only add (no custom up/down) derives its down(): on SQL it drops the added columns, on document stores it is ledger-only because up() changed no documents. The "up without down" warning does not fire for it.
dropColumn(column, { destructive: true }) (DropColumnOptions), the explicit opt-in to unset a field on a document store during a rollback.

Rollback plan: migrationRunner.planRollback(batches) returns, per migration, the tables/collections dropped or truncated and the fields/columns dropped or unset (RollbackPlan, DestructiveOperation), with document/row counts from the new optional countRows / countWithColumns driver methods (implemented for MongoDB, countRows for Postgres).

confirmRollback({ all, batches, yes, development }) prints that plan and asks for confirmation outside development. cascade migrate:rollback and cascade migrate --fresh use it and accept --yes / -y and --force.
Migration#isDocumentStore, to guard a SQL-only drop in a hand-written down().

BREAKING On document stores (MongoDB), a plain dropColumn() / dropColumns() inside down() is skipped with a warning instead of running $unset on every document. Forward drops (up(), drop: [...]) are unchanged.

BREAKING cascade migrate:rollback and cascade migrate --fresh print a destructive-operation summary first. Outside development (NODE_ENV other than development, including unset) a rollback that removes data (table or collection drops, applied field drops) asks for confirmation, and refuses without a terminal.

agent.eval({ repeat }) runs every case several times (default 1, unchanged). Case results carry passes / repeat, per-run runs, and score and pass-rate intervals; reports carry stats (overall and per EvalCase.category, Wilson intervals for pass rates and Student-t intervals for mean scores), plus stableFailures and flakyCases when repeat > 1. toJUnit shows passed 2/3 runs for repeated cases.

gate: "interval" for baseline comparison flags a case, or an overall or per-category pass rate or mean score, only when the baseline interval lies above the current interval by more than tolerance, so run-to-run noise no longer reads as a regression. The default gate: "point" keeps the existing rule. failOnStableFailures fails the regression verdict when a case failed every run. diff accepts { tolerance, gate, confidence, failOnStableFailures } as its third argument (a plain tolerance number still works), and EvalRegression gains regressedMetrics, stableFailures and flaky.
EvalCase.category groups cases for per-category statistics.
Serialized baselines store the repeat count, per-case counts and intervals; baselines saved earlier still load and count each case as one sample.

FileLog's background flush interval no longer keeps the process alive. A finished Vitest run or CLI command used to wait on it, and Vitest reported "something prevents the main process from exiting". Buffered entries are still written by flush() and flushSync().

releases.summaryHtml: Smaller, safer page payloads and the Vite 8 / Vitest 5 family. Breaking: @warlock.js/web needs Vite 8 and plugin-react 6 (a clear error names the upgrade on Vite 7), the test kit and AI matchers need Vitest 5, pages embed only the named API routes their client code reaches (config.apiRoutes, clientVisible: false), and hydration payloads carry only the translation keys a page uses. npx warlock upgrade --from 5.35 --to 5.36.0 raises Vite, Vitest and plugin-react and rewrites the Vitest 5 runner import. Shared translation groups ship once per locale as cached, content-hashed tables (fixed per process in production, with a latest-table fallback); other keys are pruned per page from literal keys, count variants, static template prefixes and config.translations, with WL9104 for keys built at run time. build.budgets.payload (default 64kb) reports oversized inline payloads by section. Fixes: development page edits no longer wait for the sitemap refresh; cascade persists unsetting a stored empty object; browser e2e click and wait errors keep the real reason near the deadline. The docs site moves to Astro 7. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.36.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: Page documents carry only the named API routes their client code can reach. The build finds them from the page's browser code (string literals, template prefixes and the register hooks of setup files) and from config.apiRoutes, which page, layout and root setups accept for names the build cannot see (a prefix.* pattern covers every name under a prefix).

build.budgets.payload sets the inline payload limit for each rendered document (default 64kb, with route globs and a warn or error mode). A runtime measurement of the hydration data and the route table, split by section, reports an over-budget route once per process with its largest keys.
warlock check reports WL9019 and WL9020 for browser route references (see core).

apiHref() and useSubmitForm({ route }) resolve names against the current page's route table. Development errors name the route and the declaration that fixes it; production throws a short error with no fallback.
A client navigation publishes the table of the page it swaps in.
The document's hydration payload no longer repeats the route table, which its own script already carries.

The client build, the development server and the Vite plugins run on Vite 8 (Rolldown) and @vitejs/plugin-react 6. The vendor split uses build.rolldownOptions with a codeSplitting group, and the development server configures JSX through oxc, so neither prints a Vite deprecation warning.
The vite peer range is ^8.0.0 and the @vitejs/plugin-react peer range is ^6.0.0.

BREAKING A page's hydration payload no longer carries every translation group, in either translation mode. It carries the keys the page's client code can reach, and the shared groups arrive in a separate, cached table. Apps that read the hydration payload directly, that read keys their client code builds at run time without declaring them, or that rely on every key being present in the browser's registry, must update. Declare the keys with config.translations, or set build.translations.prune to false in the web connector options to restore the previous payload while migrating. See the upgrade note below.

Development page edits reach the browser without waiting for the sitemap subscription refresh, which still runs in order before the next route update. Under heavy machine load a page edit made right after deleting a layout or setup file could take longer than ten seconds to appear.

Shared translation groups (default app and common) are shipped once per locale as a table whose URL carries its content hash, and the document preloads it. Hydration waits for the table, so the first client render has every key the server rendered with. Locale switching loads the other locale's table. Route dictionaries (locales.json) emit the table at build time under assets/translations/; the global registry (extend() / register()) computes it from the live registry and serves it at /__warlock/translations/<locale>.<hash>.json.
Production serves a table with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable, and each locale's newest table at /__warlock/translations/<locale>.json with no-cache.

Global-registry production builds copy the shared groups once, when the web connector boots. That copy and its hash are fixed for the process, so every process of one build publishes the same table under the same name. Keys a page registers later travel inline in its payload.

A browser whose hashed table answers 404 fetches the unhashed latest table, then retries the hashed one, and only then reports the failure and renders keys. Development serves it with no-store and carries every group, so the missing-key detector can read it. A name the server no longer holds (the eight most recent tables per locale are kept) answers 404 with no-store and never different bytes under the same name.

Per-page pruning of every other group, in both modes: a page inlines only the keys its client module graph can look up. Literal keys, static-prefix template keys (which include their subtree), module-level constants, literal choices, and config.translations declarations in the page's setup file are resolved statically. Any other key-shaped string literal in the graph (a constant, an object mapping names to keys, a prop, an argument to a helper) that equals a key, a group or a subtree is shipped too, and the head of a template literal counts as a prefix. A key used with a count ships all its variants (items_one, items_other, ...) when the page names the base. A key that cannot be resolved (trans(key), or a translator passed on as a value) makes that page fall back to every non-shared group.
The web connector's build option build.translations: sharedGroups (default ["app", "common"]) and prune (default true). Development reads the same option, so both halves share the settings.

The hydration payload's translationAssets reference (URL, hash, groups and a development flag). Client navigation merges each payload's pruned keys into the locale's dictionary (or the global registry).

Development: a translation the page reads but its payload lacks is resolved from the full table, with one warning per key and page that names the config.translations declaration to add. A base key whose count variants were delivered is not reported as missing.

Production: a missing key renders its key and is reported once through onClientError with the new kind: "translations". A shared table that cannot be loaded is retried once; the page then renders its keys and the failure is reported the same way.
warlock check reports WL9104 for a translation key computed at runtime in src/web.

Gate A's refusal of Node builtins in the bundler's external option works on Vite 8. Rolldown does not pass external to buildStart, so the guard reads the option in the options hook and normalizes a string, a RegExp, an array or a function; without this a build with fs externalized would have shipped it unrefused.
Client budget attribution (clientBudgetModules) reads Rolldown's renderedLength, and a spec runs it on a real build.

An app that still has Vite 7 installed gets a clear error before the client build or the development server starts, naming the found version and the upgrade command. Before, warlock build failed with Could not resolve entry module because Vite 7 ignores build.rolldownOptions. A Vite version that cannot be parsed is not blocked.

Named API routes are no longer published to every visitor. Admin, auth and internal endpoints are embedded only in pages whose browser code reaches them, and never for a route registered with clientVisible: false. Server-side authorization still decides each request.

clientVisible route option. Set clientVisible: false on a named API route to keep it out of every page's browser route table and out of client code. The route snapshot carries clientVisible: false only on such routes.

warlock check reports WL9019 (warning) for a browser route call (apiHref(), useSubmitForm({ route })) whose name cannot be read statically, and WL9020 (error) for a browser reference to a clientVisible: false route.
build.budgets.payload (PayloadBudget type) sets the inline payload budget for each rendered document. Web reads it; warlock build does not measure it.
page.measurePayload({ limit }) in the browser end-to-end kit records a document's inline payload under the evidence payloads.

Static translation usage analysis for the client module graph: scanTranslationSource, analyzeTranslationGraph, analyzePageTranslationUsage, readTranslationDeclarations, translationDeclarationUsage, isTranslationKeyUsed and mergeTranslationUsage. A usage lists the exact keys (each with its subtree), the static prefixes of template keys, the key-shaped string literals and template heads found anywhere in the walked modules (literals, literalPrefixes), and whether any lookup is dynamic, with the source position of each dynamic lookup. Literal keys, module-level constants, literal choices, useTrans() bindings under any local name, and config.translations declarations are resolved; a translator passed on as a value, or a key with no static prefix, is dynamic. isTranslationKeyUsed also treats a name as the base of its count variants: "cart.items" reaches cart.items_one and cart.items_other, but not cart.itemsTotal or cart.items_one.note.

WL9104: warlock check warns when a translation key in src/web is computed at runtime, because the page that renders it then ships every translation group. The warning points at the config.translations declaration that resolves it.

warlock upgrade codemod vite-8-vitest-5 (release 5.36.0): raises vite, vitest, @vitest/* and @vitejs/plugin-react in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies, overrides, resolutions), rewrites a test runner that imports VitestTestRunner from vitest/runners to TestRunner from vitest, and lists removed vitest/* entry points, a Vite config esbuild option and object manualChunks for review. A 5.36.0 note lists the Vitest 5 default changes.

warlock add test generates a runner that extends TestRunner from vitest (Vitest 5 has no vitest/runners) and declares vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 ^5.0.3. warlock add web declares vite ^8.3.3 and @vitejs/plugin-react ^6.1.2.

The browser end-to-end kit keeps the reason a target was last observed as blocking when page.click() (and the fill() and type() calls that click first) or a wait runs out of time. A CDP timeout caused by the shrinking deadline no longer replaces that reason, so the error still reads, for example, "target is covered by DIALOG#modal" instead of a CDP timeout.

The Matchers augmentation that types toRouteTo, toConverge, toPassStep and toOutputShape follows Vitest 5's Matchers<R, T> signature. With Vitest 5 installed, expect(...) keeps its custom matcher types; the augmentation no longer compiles against Vitest 4.

Unsetting a stored empty object (model.unset("field") on a field holding {}) is persisted: the model reports the change and save() issues the $unset. It was silently skipped, because an empty object has no leaves to diff; a spec only passed by reading a mock call left over from an earlier test.

The template pins Vitest 5.0.3. Selecting the test feature generates the runner against Vitest 5's TestRunner, and a web project declares Vite 8 and @vitejs/plugin-react 6. The generator's own dev dependencies use @types/node 22, the minimum Vitest 5 supports.

releases.summaryHtml: Design system, web generators, new check rules, API helpers, budgets, accessibility tests and faster test runs. Breaking: root components now run in the browser so hydration covers the full document ancestry (move server-only root work to the root setup loader), and model resources receive hidden columns with hidden enforced on final output. warlock add design-system scaffolds fourteen accessible shadcn controls wired to Mongez React Form, included by default in full-stack and Tailwind + shadcn starters; warlock generate page, form and crud-ui scaffold pages, forms and guarded CRUD screens. warlock check adds WL9013–WL9018 (component size, component-owned state, native controls and validation, controllers without a response schema) and --fix; warlock inspect --section files and warlock explain <file> map files, imports and the routes that reach them. Core adds AppError, listEndpoint, assertResponseContracts, per-page gzip build budgets and page.assertAccessible() with axe-core; tests gain opt-in worker lifetime, setupTest({ mode: "unit" }) and setup profiling. Auth bounds Google and JWKS requests; web keeps sessions in sync after refresh, locale changes and page swaps. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.35.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: Typed AppError domain failures with native HTTP handling and http.errorResponse context, preserving legacy HTTP error behavior.
listEndpoint builds typed plural-key page responses from validated query controls and repository list callbacks, with bounded limits and explicit sort/filter whitelists.
assertResponseContracts checks real HTTP responses against declared status schemas, with fixtures, resource support and optional complete status coverage.
