Web convention warnings for component size, multiple components, component-owned state/effects and handlers, native form controls and native validation; exported controller response schema warnings (WL9013–WL9018). Configure severity and component line limits through .warlock-check.json.
warlock check --fix applies safe relative import extension fixes and exposes available edits through the optional JSON fix field.

warlock inspect --section files lists every file under src/ with its module, convention role, exports and resolved import graph without booting the app. The versioned report schema and MCP inspect_files tool expose the same section.
warlock explain <file> prints exports, importers and transitively reaching routes/pages, with --json support. Error-code explanations continue to work.

Per-page gzip JS/CSS build budgets with route overrides, warn/error enforcement, previous-build deltas, and warlock build --json reports. Existing apps remain report-only unless limits are configured.
Browser page.assertAccessible(options?) using a pinned local axe-core injection over CDP, exact rule/selector allowances, violation diagnostics and accessibility evidence.

Opt-in tests.lifetime: "worker" for Vitest forks in a single run with a shared module graph (isolate: false) and the generated cleanup runner. Connectors boot once per worker, file boundaries reset fakes/clock/IDs/private storage and await tests.resetBetweenFiles, and worker cleanup awaits shutdown. getTestRuntimeStats() exposes bootstrap/file counts. Unsafe pools, watch, isolation and missing runner configurations are refused.
setupTest({ mode: "unit", importModule }) loads configuration values once per module graph without bootstrap hooks, config special handlers, connectors, fake installation or native loader hooks.

tests.profileSetup / WARLOCK_TEST_PROFILE=1 report setup steps and teardown per file, with summaries per worker including final shutdown; the generated TestSetupReporter aggregates a run summary across workers. setupTest({ file }) labels profiles.

recommendedTestWorkers() from @warlock.js/core/vite respects CPU affinity and visible cgroup v2 CPU quotas. Testing docs/skills cover shared HTTP/database contention and affected-tests plus integration release gates, with a full suite nightly.

warlock add design-system scaffolds app-owned accessible shadcn controls connected to Mongez React Form, with pinned dependencies, a Tailwind preflight before mutations, preservation of existing files, and dry-run support.
warlock generate page <path> scaffolds a UI-only page and setup companion with route, loader and metadata; --interactive adds a feature hook.

warlock generate form <name> [--module <name>] [--endpoint] scaffolds design-system controls, a shared Seal schema, a useSubmitForm hook and an optional guarded controller/route with validation and response schema.

warlock generate crud-ui <module> scaffolds guarded list/create/edit pages, schema-backed forms, endpoint-derived filters, pagination and a delete action for conventional CRUD modules. All web generators support dry-run JSON reports and preserve existing files unless forced.
Document the development devtools captured-mail preview without logging message bodies.
warlock check --changed includes transitive import dependents for scoped lint, conventions and related tests. Changed typecheck diagnostics now include transitive importers.

New warlock add test configs split pure *.spec.ts files from integration *.test.ts and specs under tests/; only integration loads framework/HTTP setup. Existing configs are preserved. The generated runner requires Vitest 4.1.10 or newer.

Reference workload before this change: 1,335 files, 3,532.79 seconds summed setup, 4,465.55 seconds wall time (reported on 5.33.0). No after measurement was run under the implementation check-once rule. The startup cost model changes from one bootstrap per file to one per active worker plus reset cost; this is not a measured wall-time speedup. Use the new profiling switch to compare the same suite and worker count.
Restore application-config-only preload for feature generators, preserving configured notification locales and one-shot CLI exit. Correct cleanup test hooks to return void.

Fix CRUD UI generation with the Oxc parser, ES2022-compatible tooling arrays, nullable component bodies, and app-free feature scaffolding. Align inspection CLI tests and convention error-code headings.
Wait for owned MessagePort close events in the test-server disposal regression so referenced handles are actually released.
Recognize required and optional auth descriptors in route inspection and generated agent summaries, including inherited session guards.
Describe optional authentication as an anonymous security alternative in OpenAPI while keeping legacy guards required.
Generate notification locale strings for every configured locale with an explicit English fallback.
Exclude co-located tests and test-only directories from configuration discovery and reload.
Register module JSON dictionaries in each test worker and remove them during teardown.
Dispose HTTP test-server file runtime resources and pending loader acknowledgements on shutdown and failed startup.
Native ESM loader registration shares a process-global promise across repeated initialization and module reloads; test startup skips the hook when an importer runs application modules through Vitest.

Add the build-rtl-and-mixed-direction-ui and preserve-feedback-and-motion agent skill topics, covering RTL layouts and mixed-direction content, and accessible feedback, failure handling and motion patterns.

Client manifest traversal for first-visit and deferred asset sizes, including hydration, page layouts, setup registrations and error boundaries; Rollup module attribution identifies the largest contributors.
Watched development regression coverage for shared-store connectivity and a characterization of layout form identifier hydration parity.

build-accessible-controls skill and design-system documentation cover shared Mongez controls, keyboard and focus behavior, stable ids, RTL, visual checked states, empty/reset semantics, and calendar dates versus instants.
Correct the ClientOnly opening example to defer browser reads through a function child, and update the navigation and page-guard skill examples to match the real API.
Production builds no longer fail the client budget report when a setup file has no browser register hook; its empty projection adds no bytes.
Carry resolved document slots through the shared hydration payload so navigation data and document-embedded payloads stay identical.
Include generated guarded-route output in the page protection skill so its session and useUser examples compile independently.

BREAKING Hydrate the same full-document root ancestry as SSR, preserving React useId() and generated form IDs beneath layouts. Root components now execute in the browser; move server-only work to root setup loaders. Client navigation continues to replace the layout/page subtree inside #vessel.
Install fetched sessions on refresh, locale changes, and central page swaps, including guest sessions; superseded responses cannot publish identity.
Preserve the shared request-store resolver and request-keyed scopes across server module re-evaluation during development.
New projects configure gzip client budgets of 150kb JavaScript and 50kb CSS, enforced by warlock build.
Web starter home-page browser spec with accessibility, overflow and screenshot checks at phone and desktop widths; omitted from API-only projects.

Pin the template's Vitest to 4.1.10 for awaited worker cleanup support. Selecting the test feature uses core's unit/integration projects generator, including quota-aware worker sizing and the cleanup runner, while preserving existing configs.

Update the testing-strategy project skill and scaffolding docs with matching file conventions, cheap unit configuration, opt-in worker lifetime/reset hooks, setup profiling and an affected-tests plus integration release gate with full suites nightly.

Full-stack and Tailwind + shadcn selections include fourteen accessible app-owned form controls, separate behavior hooks and props types, and exact UI dependency pins. The optional template and add-command payload share an integrity contract.
Template web standards name the shared controls and their direct web-alias imports; template verification includes the optional sources.
Add a state ownership rule to the web code standards skill: loader data is server truth, and shared client state lives in named store modules.

Teach the project API design skill to use typed domain errors, bounded list endpoints and response-schema contract assertions. The starter formatter preserves explicitly safe AppError messages and details through its native typed context.

Keep the existing-Tailwind design controls label within narrow terminal rows and supply the ResizeObserver test adapter needed by Radix form inputs in jsdom, and complete async submission fixtures before resubmitting. Pin matching React and React DOM test dependencies for standalone runs.
Restore session middleware response fixtures, keep session projection defaults typed as unknown, and skip renewal without an explicit user type.
Exclude expired refresh rows from session caps while preserving oldest-first eviction.
Bound Google token and JWKS requests with configurable timeoutMs, fetch and endpoints options; retain all identity checks and isolate JWKS caches.
Reject unavailable refresh families outside the transaction callback so expected credential rejection is not logged as a database failure.
Publish required/optional session guard descriptors and markers for grouped route inspection.
BREAKING Model resources receive hidden columns for public field derivations; hidden is enforced on final resource output instead of its input.

Every package exports exactly one skill named after it, with package-level descriptions of at most 450 characters (about 13,300 characters in total, down from 22,900). New apps get revised project skills: single-responsibility components, Mongez React Form validation only, custom accessible controls on the project's UI kit, camelCase response fields, { error: { code, message } } errors, responseSchema and Idempotency-Key guidance, and Oxlint rules that enforce them. Core adds the opt-in http.errorResponse formatter for every JSON error, ResponseStatus gains 413 and 422, and warlock e2e gains browser.startupTimeoutMs (default 30 seconds). releases.summaryHtml: Page setup files become the documented way to add page logic, plus MCP and secrets fixes. A page's config, loader, register and action/actions live in its *.setup.ts file and its UI file holds only components; metadata always lives in config.metadata. A new Page setup files guide, and every web docs example, skill, the starter template and the page/layout/root generators follow it; the setup-file error lists every allowed export. ai-tools: tools from a remote MCP server now show the model their real input schema (Standard JSON Schema), and ai.mcp.serve HTTP transports accept onAuthRefusal to keep an app's own auth-error response, with Host/Origin checks unchanged. Core: secrets.backend() reports whether the keychain, encrypted-file or memory backend is active, reusing core's own selection. Docs: tables in MDX pages render again. No breaking changes. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.34.1 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: HTTP transport.onAuthRefusal customizes denied authentication responses for the MCP endpoint and side routes using typed safe context, 4xx/5xx statuses, allowlisted headers and JSON bodies. Host/Origin guards retain precedence, invalid or throwing hooks retain the default refusal, and handlers never run after a denial.

Tools adapted from a remote MCP server now show the model their real input schema. jsonSchemaToStandard implements Standard JSON Schema (~standard.jsonSchema), so extractJsonSchema and every provider adapter read the server's inputSchema instead of falling back to a parameterless { type: "object" }, which made models guess argument names and retry. Adapters receive copies of the schema; a tool without one advertises { type: "object", properties: {} }.

Async secrets.backend() and SecretStore.backend() report "keychain", "file" or "memory" without credentials, sharing lazy selection and its memoized keychain probe. Resolved driver configuration, environment lookups and injected backend metadata have documented reporting semantics; memory fakes report "memory" without probing.
Generate root.setup.ts and index.setup.ts with Web starter policy and universal registration, keeping the UI files focused on components.
List all five allowed setup exports (config, loader, register, action, actions) in composition errors.
Correct Web documentation and skills to keep page, layout, root, and error logic in setup files, with metadata in config.metadata; add a complete page setup guide.
Document setup-file ownership in the Web starter and its code standards; retain metadata in config.metadata and cover UI/setup pairs in template integrity specs.

releases.summaryHtml: ESLint and Prettier support removed, plus multi-file transactions, browser end-to-end tests, an AI tool catalogue, a local queue driver and MCP serving hooks. The ESLint checker, --lint eslint, devServer.healthCheckers.eslint and Prettier scripts are gone; each removed option fails with a message naming 5.34.0, and no published package depends on ESLint or Prettier. warlock upgrade --from 5.33 --to 5.34.0 migrates apps and now ports custom ESLint rules to Oxlint where an equivalent exists, reporting the rest; new and migrated apps enable Oxlint's correctness rules, and npm apps with a pnpm-workspace.yaml get the right install hint. fs: fs.transaction() stages multi-file writes with read-your-writes, hash or epoch preconditions, a durable journal with crash recovery, operation-id replay and consistent reads. Core: warlock e2e and @warlock.js/core/e2e drive Chrome or Edge over the DevTools protocol with hit-tested clicks, overflow checks at 1280 and 390 px, console and network checks, evidence and PID-verified teardown; an in-memory secrets backend for built-app tests. AI: ai.tools.catalogue() advertises a small core plus governed search and call meta-tools; ai.mcp.serve adds listFilter, HTTP transport.routes, validateCallParams and keeps McpError codes. Queue: driver: "local" (SQLite via node:sqlite, no Redis) and driver: "memory". Seal: v.record(key, value). Web: refresh events carry a reason, and shared data stays fresh across shell swaps. Breaking: ESLint/Prettier removal, Oxlint correctness rules, v.object() refuses arrays and non-plain objects. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.34.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: Select an isolated in-memory secrets backend through SECRETS_DRIVER=memory or secrets.driver, including built-server test deployments and explicit SecretStore options. Configuration overrides the environment; unknown drivers fail closed.

Refuse the memory driver under NODE_ENV=production unless allowMemoryInProduction: true is explicitly configured; preserve log masking and namespace isolation without keychain/environment/file access.

Add warlock e2e and the isolated @warlock.js/core/e2e Node subpath: owned app/build fixtures and browser profiles, direct CDP with native WebSocket, stable hit-tested clicks, editable text and navigation waits, responsive screenshots and overflow assertions, console/network allowlists, per-run evidence and PID-verified process-group cleanup. Include fake-CDP coverage, real-browser integration specs and a complete browser-testing guide/skill.

oxc-toolchain-removal runs on warlock upgrade --from 5.33 --to 5.34.0, reusing the preserved 5.33 oxc-toolchain migration. It ports literal folder restrictions, native TypeScript rule equivalents, unused-import checks, globals and ignores; unsupported rules/options report their source and file scope without executing config. Native type-aware equivalents enable the optional app engine automatically.
BREAKING Migrated template configs enable Oxlint correctness: error; stale literal healthCheckers.eslint options are removed.
Detect a real lockfile beside pnpm-workspace.yaml before treating the directory as pnpm. npm apps with only package-lock.json now receive the correct install hint.
Validate Postman draft-04 schemas with an explicit development-only Ajv adapter instead of resolving ESLint's private dependency. Generated source formatting checks use Oxfmt.

BREAKING Remove the ESLint development checker, CLI selection, checker config option and production dependency. warlock check --lint eslint now fails with the 5.34.0 removal and Oxlint/Oxfmt migration guidance.

ai.mcp.serve supports async listFilter(context, tools) for per-request discovery independent of callability, and validateCallParams(context, params) for application envelope policy before lookup, schema validation and call policy, over HTTP and stdio. Default handling of unknown fields and unsupported task metadata is unchanged.

HTTP transport.routes adds exact method/path application routes beneath the MCP URL with shared authentication, principal/context, Host/Origin guards, body limits, disconnect signals and shutdown draining. Conflicting or invalid route configuration fails before binding.
Export McpError(code, message, data?) and the new discovery, envelope and HTTP route contracts.

beforeCall and envelope policy preserve a thrown McpError's integer code, message and optional data, including official SDK errors, without a runtime SDK dependency. Other throws retain the existing invalid-params mapping.
Extend the core ai.tools namespace on registration, preserving catalogue and measure while adding the ready-made factories. AiToolsNamespace remains re-exported for consumers.

Select driver: "local" for durable single-host SQLite queues using Node's built-in node:sqlite without Redis, or driver: "memory" for tests executing real handlers. Existing configuration defaults to BullMQ.
A shared QueueDriver contract and getQueueDriver() for dispatch, snapshots, failed-job recovery, and worker lifecycle across all backends.
Local/memory delays, priorities, retries with fixed/exponential backoff, retention, per-queue concurrency, context propagation, progress, and results through the existing defineJob() API.

Transactional claims, renewable fenced leases, recovery after worker crashes, and bounded graceful shutdown releasing unfinished local jobs. Local/memory handlers receive an optional cancellation signal.

v.record(keyValidator, valueValidator, errorMessage?) validates original property names and values, infers partial literal-key dictionaries, and emits key JSON Schema. Existing value-only and error-message forms remain supported.
BREAKING v.object() requires a plain or null-prototype object; arrays, built-ins, class instances and custom prototypes fail even with unknown-key options enabled.
Reject malformed record validator arguments at schema definition with a clear TypeError.
Remove the remaining ESLint, Prettier and typescript-eslint development dependencies; package linting and formatting use Oxlint/Oxfmt.

fs.transaction and fs.openTransactions: root-scoped multi-file staging with read-your-writes, content-hash/root-epoch preconditions, process ownership, durable intent journals, automatic roll-forward recovery and operation-id result replay.

Read-only fs.inspectTransactions, bounded epoch-checked fs.read, and root-bound read / readMany for consistent snapshots. Document single-host cooperating-process limits and explicit file-only durability on Windows.

Optional atomicWriteAsync(path, content, { durability: "file" | "full" }) flushes file bytes before rename and, with full durability, directory entries afterward. Existing unflushed defaults remain unchanged.
Validate supervisor configuration before accessing options; errors name the missing or invalid owner or registry option.
Strip guardian ownership and launch variables from macOS/Windows workload environments, including Windows casing aliases. Guardian proof remains intact; Linux retains its /proc ownership token.

Refresh lifecycle events carry a reason distinguishing explicit refreshes from live-data, polling/reconnect and focus revalidation. Export RefreshReason and RefreshOptions; allow app-owned background refresh({ reason }) calls.
Seal and publish each successful page/shell swap's shared snapshot at the central swap boundary, updating retained useShared() consumers.

BREAKING Enable Oxlint correctness: error in the only app template. Move the footer's year calculation outside render to satisfy its purity check. Standalone specs use locally declared, pinned Oxlint/Oxfmt tools.

BREAKING Remove the ESLint/Prettier scaffold, prompt, configs, dependencies and TypeScript 6.0.3 compatibility pin. --lint eslint fails before scaffolding and names 5.34.0 and the Oxlint/Oxfmt default. Remove Prettier compatibility scripts and validation paths.

ai.tools.catalogue({ core, searchable, limit?, searchName?, callName? }) (also catalogue) keeps a stable advertised core plus bounded schema search and governed hidden calls. Supports deterministic name/description/tag ranking, lazy cached tool loading, provider-tool passthrough, durable inventory drift detection and measurement with ai.measure / ai.tools.measure. Hidden calls resolve before the normal agent tool pipeline so target validation, policy, HITL, accounting, context and tracing remain intact.
Remove the remaining ESLint and Prettier development dependencies; package linting and formatting use Oxlint/Oxfmt.

releases.summaryHtml: Oxlint + Oxfmt become the only default toolchain, plus MCP request context, live page data, app-scoped secrets, AI measurement, PM2 commands and a new process supervisor. ESLint and Prettier are off by default and deprecated (removal in 5.34.0): an ESLint config alone no longer enables checks, and warlock upgrade --from 5.32 --to 5.33.0 migrates an app to Oxlint/Oxfmt. AI: ai.mcp.serve passes requestId, an authenticated principal and cancellation signals to tools, with beforeCall policy after input validation; ai.measure() and warlock ai measure report per-part input tokens and cost, with measure.diff. Web: pages opt into config.live for loader refreshes pushed over sockets with polling fallback, driven by invalidatePageCache(tags). Core: secrets.get/set/remove/has with OS keychain, scoped environment and encrypted-file backends and log masking; warlock pm2 init/reload with PM2 readiness after boot. Devtools: an AI panel on Panoptic traces and a Processes panel. New package @warlock.js/process (warlock add process) supervises app-owned workers on Linux, macOS and Windows with token and start-time identity, group stops and memory caps. Breaking: ESLint/Prettier no longer selected automatically, MCP cancellation and policy order, secret fakes in default test setup. Lockstep release across all 33 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.33.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: Add application-owned process supervision with random environment tokens, PID/start-time registry identity, safe group stops, label filtering, boot recovery and shutdown cleanup.
Expose streamed worker handles, exit reasons and peak memory; lazily load optional node-pty for terminals.
Support macOS without custom native code: parse ps start time under LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC and verify the inherited random environment token through a live Node launch guardian.

Support Windows with PowerShell/CIM creation identity, the guardian's inherited token, PID-only taskkill /T /F tree stops, tree working-set polling, timeouts, recovery and optional node-pty/ConPTY terminals. Job Objects remain a future improvement.

Make platform command construction, parsing and launch plans pure and observation injectable for Linux-hosted macOS/Windows specs; reject truly unsupported operating systems with UnsupportedProcessPlatformError.

Attempt Linux cgroup v2 before user code executes, with inherited rlimit/RSS fallback; document softer macOS rlimit/tree RSS and Windows tree RSS enforcement, guardian memory overhead and POSIX-only CPU limits.
Integrate warlock add process and a read-only devtools process panel.

oxc-toolchain, a 5.33.0 warlock upgrade codemod, migrates generated configs, package scripts/dependencies, editor settings and literal dev health switches to Oxlint/Oxfmt. Customized files are retained with file:line review guidance; additions and deletions honor --dry-run and --json.
BREAKING ESLint no longer starts from config detection alone in the dev server or warlock check. TypeScript and configured Oxlint remain the default health checkers; check defaults to Oxlint.

Completed application boot now sends PM2's "ready" IPC message without disconnecting its channel; the existing warlock start readiness protocol remains supported. Cluster workers skip the exclusive port preflight so they can share their primary's listener during rolling reloads.
Type the socket connector’s raw HTTP(S) server across asynchronous listener startup; keep native-keyring test doubles declaration-safe and cover the documented check --lint option.
Socket-only connector boot awaits its listener and rejects bind failures before application readiness can be announced.
ESLint/Prettier support is removed in 5.34.0. Explicit ESLint opt-ins emit one deprecation warning per process on stderr with migration instructions.

AI panel at /__warlock and AI runs in HTTP request details, powered by optional @warlock.js/ai-panoptic: model, token/cache usage, historical cost, provider cache-hit trips, tool timings, retries, truncation and compaction metadata.
Read-only AI list/detail endpoints and ai stream updates behind the existing development/loopback guard, with install guidance when Panoptic is unavailable.
Bounded content-free trace retention, request-local correlation and cleanup with the dashboard Clear action and connector shutdown; application exporter/cache stores remain independent.
Add a read-only Processes panel and guarded /api/processes endpoint, discovering the application registration generated by warlock add process only in development.

Page-owned config.live: { tags, pollInterval } re-runs matching loader pipelines after invalidatePageCache broadcasts through core's Socket.IO adapter. configureLivePageData({ socket }) reuses an app-owned client and falls back to polling without a connected socket.

Live updates wait for navigation and unsent <Form> input, discard in-flight responses when editing begins, and bypass page caches. Document shared-cache/socket-adapter requirements for multiple processes and publishing workers.
Use root Oxlint/Oxfmt binaries and configuration for package lint/fix and format scripts. Legacy ESLint/Prettier dependencies and configs remain until the 5.34.0 removal.

Keep live-refresh cleanup free of control-flow overrides, exercise relative navigation URLs in the live-refresh regression, and demonstrate binding an application-owned socket without an undeclared client import.
ToolContext adds optional requestId and principal fields for server transports, keeping authenticated identity out of tool input and model messages.

ai.measure({ model, tools?, system?, messages?, skills? }) and standalone measure report per-part native input token counts or labelled estimates and uncached input USD when priced. measure.diff(before, after) returns signed per-part and total changes with the original reports. Includes compact schemas, catalogue-only measurement, explicit probe metadata, and whole-report fallback for unsupported count shapes.
Use root Oxlint/Oxfmt binaries and configuration for package lint/fix and format scripts. Legacy ESLint/Prettier dependencies and configs remain until the 5.34.0 removal.

subscribeTraces(listener) and TraceListener for process-local adapters observing finalized traces from every built-in collector before exporter dispatch, with isolated listener failures and independent teardown.
Optional Trace.requestId and exact TraceQuery.requestId filters for both in-memory and cache-backed query/aggregate APIs.

Content-free retry-attempt timings, provider cache-hit and truncated-trip counts, agent compaction decisions and provider compaction-block counts on trace attributes, surfaced by the devtools AI panel.

MCP serving now exposes per-call requestId, authenticated principal and cancellation-aware signals over HTTP and stdio. HTTP auth.authenticate resolves principals alongside bearer/authorize checks; stdio accepts static or provider principals. beforeCall validates policy after input validation and can return a native error refusal or throw a JSON-RPC error. notifications/cancelled aborts only the matching caller/request and suppresses its response. New hook/context/refusal and stdio transport types are exported.
Keep HTTP and MCP fixtures valid under strict indexed access, accept string JSON-RPC request IDs in serving tests, and replace stdin through its descriptor without pretending a stream is a terminal.

Label the explicit ESLint/Prettier prompt choice, flag help and docs as deprecated; retain TypeScript 6.0.3 compatibility and explicitly enable its dev-server checker. Package development scripts use root Oxlint/Oxfmt, and the template formatting gate defaults to Oxfmt. Oxc scripts explicitly select .oxfmtignore.
--lint=eslint prints a clear removal warning for 5.34.0, recommends --lint=oxc and names the existing-app migration command. Explicit Prettier compatibility scripts also warn.
Use root Oxlint/Oxfmt binaries and configuration for package lint/fix and format scripts. Legacy ESLint/Prettier dependencies and configs remain until the 5.34.0 removal.
Use root Oxlint/Oxfmt binaries and configuration for package lint/fix and format scripts. Legacy ESLint/Prettier dependencies and configs remain until the 5.34.0 removal.

Add registerLogSecret(value, keys?) and maskRegisteredLogSecrets(text) for process-lifetime credential masking. Registered keys and literal values remain protected with defaults disabled or custom censors, including free text, Error causes and channel failure diagnostics. The safety pass masks opaque objects and does not invoke serializers/getters.
Use root Oxlint/Oxfmt binaries and configuration for package lint/fix and format scripts. Legacy ESLint/Prettier dependencies and configs remain until the 5.34.0 removal.

releases.summaryHtml: TypeScript 7 across the family, metric-matched web fonts, and fixes from upgrading real apps to 5.31. Every package, new app and the release tooling move to TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native tsc): the workspace typecheck drops from about 1 min 51 s to 36 s, warlock typecheck/check and the dev-server checker run on the native compiler, and syntax analysis uses oxc-parser. Apps drop baseUrl and moduleResolution: node/node10 from their tsconfig. New apps default to Oxlint + Oxfmt; the opt-in ESLint toolchain stays on TypeScript 6.0.3 because typescript-eslint does not support TypeScript 7. Web: declared fonts with preload, metric-matched fallbacks that stop the layout shift when a web font swaps in, and immutable caching. AI: opt-in native MCP results, private permissions for snapshot/session/cassette files, Gemini Developer API token counting with system prompts and tools (with an estimate fallback), hosted-search usage and cost across providers, Qwen search and Kimi search/fetch tools. Security: esbuild 0.28.2 (GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr). Notifications imports herald as an optional peer instead of bundling a private copy. Agents get report-framework-issue.md and warlock issue to file framework issues with consent. Breaking: TypeScript 7 config changes, private AI file modes, herald must be installed for .queue() with the herald backend. Lockstep release across all 32 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.32.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: warlock issue [--type bug|feature] [--title "..."] [--json] collects installed environment details and a static config summary without booting the app, then prints a bounded pre-filled framework issue URL; it never submits anything. Add bug/feature issue forms and the report-framework-issue.md agent topic with minimal-repro, privacy, duplicate-search and user-consent guidance.

Clarify the upgrade skill: new scaffolds default to Oxlint/Oxfmt and TypeScript 7.0.2; explicit ESLint mode stays on TypeScript 6.0.3 to satisfy typescript-eslint, with deprecation planned for 5.33 and removal for 5.34.

Verify generated web stubs with the scaffold’s TypeScript-independent Prettier import sorter, including an explicit no-plugin negative control and decorator parsing; align the contact controller stub’s inline type-specifier order.

BREAKING: pin typescript to 7.0.2, whose tsc command uses the native Go compiler. Apps must remove baseUrl, rebase paths, replace moduleResolution: "node" / "node10", and declare ambient Node types explicitly.
Preserve incremental CLI checks and changed-file filtering; reuse a native compiler session for per-file development diagnostics and close it on shutdown.
Parse imports, configuration, translation keys, model/resource typings, convention checks, page discovery and doctor migrations with OXC instead of the removed JavaScript compiler API.
Fix source development workers on Node.js 24 failing to load Node builtins through native dependencies, restoring background TypeScript health checks.
Upgrade esbuild to ^0.28.2, past the Windows development-server advisory GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr (patched in 0.28.1).

Declare self-hosted fonts once with typed web.fonts: generated font-face CSS and variables, critical preloads in buffered and streamed heads, page/layout/root preload opt-outs, and metric-matched local fallbacks. Dependency-free sfnt/WOFF/WOFF2 metrics use Capsize's recorded system metrics and weighted Latin advances to reduce layout shifts when a condensed display font swaps into a hero heading.

Declared font files and their stylesheet are hashed Vite assets with the existing one-year immutable production cache. Development caches metrics and warns about TTF/OTF files and critical faces missing preload or fallback.
Pin the package development compiler to TypeScript 7.0.2 and use explicit Node types and source roots with supported module resolution.
Upgrade esbuild to ^0.28.2, past the Windows development-server advisory GHSA-g7r4-m6w7-qqqr (patched in 0.28.1).

Provider-reported hosted-tool usage counters, per-request ModelPricing.serverTools rates and historical cost.serverTools amounts; mergeUsage and totalCost include them. Budget reserve mode accepts serverToolRequests with fail-closed fee pricing. Responses and streaming terminal chunks retain raw provider metadata; agent trips retain metadata and handle adapter-supplied hosted continuations within maxTrips without function dispatch.
ai.snapshot.file({ dir, dirMode?, fileMode? }) accepts custom permission modes with private defaults, refusing invalid modes and group/other write bits.
Update provider-tool guidance to use the first-party Kimi search/fetch client tools and their usage accounting, replacing the unreleased builtin path retiring on 20 October 2026.
Pin the package development compiler to TypeScript 7.0.2 and use explicit Node types and source roots with supported module resolution.

countInputTokens falls back to a full-input estimate when native counting explicitly signals InvalidRequestError.reason: "count-unsupported", keeping reserve-mode budget preflight usable with unsupported request shapes while propagating real provider errors.

Local snapshot and VCR cassette stores create directories with 0700 and JSON files with exactly 0600, including temporary files before atomic rename and rewrites of older files. Existing directories are never chmod-ed. SQLite path stores create private parents and set the database and journal/WAL/SHM sidecars to 0600; caller-supplied database connections retain caller-managed permissions. POSIX modes are ignored on Windows.

BREAKING: the default scaffold toolchain is now Oxlint + Oxfmt (--lint=oxc) with TypeScript 7.0.2. Explicit --lint=eslint retains ESLint + Prettier with TypeScript 6.0.3 so npm, pnpm and yarn can satisfy typescript-eslint's peer range. The wizard, help and headless defaults agree.

ESLint selection prints one compatibility notice explaining the TypeScript 6.0.3 pin and planned deprecation in 5.33 / removal in 5.34. The scaffold gate accepts --lint and --pm to verify both toolchains with npm, pnpm or yarn; CI exercises Oxc by default.

Replace the Prettier import organizer with @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports so import sorting works with TypeScript 7. Keep built-ins, packages, internal aliases and relative imports in one block, with separate type imports; align Oxfmt’s internal-alias groups with the same template source. Formatters retain unused imports; ESLint or Oxlint reports them.

BREAKING: scaffold the default Oxlint/Oxfmt mode with TypeScript 7.0.2 using the native tsc command, supported tsconfig options and explicit Node types. Existing apps must remove baseUrl, rebase paths, and replace classic Node module resolution.

Document the optional ESLint parser's dependence on the removed JavaScript compiler API; keep its compiler isolated in the monorepo's development tooling so ESLint specs remain executable while the default scaffold uses TS7.

Export kimiSearchTool() (Basic/Pro), kimiFetchTool() and verified KIMI_SERVER_TOOL_PRICING: authenticated, cancellable first-party REST calls with compact results, mapped errors, no automatic retries, and billable response usage/costs aggregated into agent reports.
