releases.summaryHtml: Rate limits that actually apply in production, a toolbelt for AI coding agents, and a broad AI upgrade. Security: the global HTTP rate limiter (http.rateLimit, 60 requests/minute per IP by default) is now enforced in production — in 5.30 and earlier it never applied to application routes; static files and the /health//ready probes are exempt by default. Agents get warlock inspect --json, warlock check (typecheck, lint, related tests and framework convention checks with stable WLxxxx codes and an environment-vs-code exit split), warlock explain, warlock mcp, warlock trace, a generated app AGENTS.md, warlock board, warlock make endpoint, --dry-run --json on every generator, a test kit with fakes on by default and model factories, and warlock upgrade codemods. AI: a run cut off by the output or context limit ends as AgentIncompleteError instead of an empty success, cost is cache-aware with verified price tables and reserve-then-commit budgets, reasoning/tool-argument/usage stream chunks, provider-defined tools, conversation sessions with file and SQLite stores, compaction for thinking runs, MCP serving over HTTP with auth, a coding-agent workspace tool belt, and the new @warlock.js/ai-cli that drives 14 vendor coding CLIs as agents. Also: built apps start on Bun and Deno (warlock dev stays on Node), Node 22.15 is the minimum, a confined no-follow reader in @warlock.js/fs, FileLog naming and retention, route-level validation failure responses, and v.union tries every matching object member. Breaking: enforced rate limits, incomplete agent runs, v.union error paths, sortable FileLog names, and more — see the upgrade notes and warlock upgrade --from 5.30 --to 5.31.0. Lockstep release across all 32 packages, one of them new (@warlock.js/ai-cli). Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.31.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, every package was confirmed at the npm origin and the blog check passed against npm.

items.html: @warlock.js/core/net: a side-effect-free subpath exporting the SSRF IP classifier isPrivateOrReservedIp (the same function the root exports). It loads only node:net, so workers, CLIs and standalone processes — @warlock.js/ai among them — can reuse the private-address rules without loading the HTTP server, database, cache or mail modules behind the root entry.

http.rateLimit.staticFiles (default false) decides whether static files count against the global rate limiter. Each static mount can decide for itself: router.directory(options, { rateLimit }) and a fourth { rateLimit } argument on router.file(), cachedFile(), files() and cachedFiles() take true (global limiter), false (exempt) or { max, timeWindow, errorMessage? } (own limit and bucket).

Route validation can answer with an application's own failure body. validation.onFailure(result, { request, response, route }) returns { status?, body } for a failed schema or params (no status uses validation.response.status, 422 by default); validation.response.body(result, route) in the validation config does the same for every route. The route hook wins, either may return undefined to fall through, and the framework body is unchanged when neither is set. Routes also accept a validation option merged over the handler's own, so one handler can serve several routes with different failure codes. ValidationConfiguration now types response and responseStatus.

warlock generate.openapi documents a custom validation failure body from the handler's responseSchema entry for the failure status instead of the framework's ValidationFailed shape; without one, the configured status is documented without a body and a route-level hook produces a warning.
evaluateConditionalRequest(), matchesIfNoneMatch(), matchesIfMatch() and parseEntityTagList() expose the framework's RFC 9110 precondition handling for application handlers that set their own ETags.
A route's rateLimit option also accepts false to exempt the route from the global limiter, and true to keep it under the global policy (the default for application routes).

Production runtime support for Bun and Deno. An app built on Node with warlock build starts and serves on Bun 1.4.3 and Deno 2.9.7, either directly (bun dist/app.js, deno run -A dist/app.js) or through warlock start run with that runtime. A runtimes CI workflow builds a fixture app with pages, API routes, file cache, file logging and static files from the packed framework, starts it on Node, Bun and Deno, and checks every route plus a clean SIGTERM shutdown. The "Supported runtimes" docs page lists the commands for each runtime.

detectJavaScriptRuntime(), describeJavaScriptRuntime(), nodeOnlyCommandError(), assertNodeOnlyCommand() and unverifiedBuildRuntimeNotice() report which runtime is executing ({ type: "node" | "bun" | "deno", version }), and let a CLI command refuse to run anywhere but Node.

warlock inspect [--json] [--section routes,models,…] prints the app's facts from its booted registries: routes (middleware chain, auth guard, CSRF, rate limit, logging, request/response JSON Schema), models (table, columns, relations, resource), resources, config keys with types (never values), event listeners, pages (layout chain, loaders, actions, guard), queue jobs, scheduled tasks and installed @warlock.js/* versions. Boots like warlock doctor — no connection, no port. The report is versioned (schemaVersion: 1, fields only ever added) and published as JSON Schema: schemas/inspect-report.schema.json and INSPECT_REPORT_JSON_SCHEMA. inspectApp() returns the same object inside any process where the app is booted; bootForInspect() boots first.

warlock check [--changed] [--base <ref>] [--skip …] [--json] is one verify command: an incremental typecheck (in a child process, so running out of memory is reported), the app's ESLint/oxlint, the tests the change affects (vitest run / vitest related), and convention checks (importing an auto-loaded file, .js import extensions, relative imports across modules, experimentalDecorators). One JSON object per problem — { code, category, severity, source, file, line, column, message, hint, skill, docs, rule } — and exit codes that split your code (1) from this machine (2: Node version, missing tool, unreachable database/Redis, busy port, git unavailable, tool crash). It detects and reports only; it never stops processes or frees ports.

warlock check's conventions step also reports security and code-style problems from source, the same with ESLint, Oxlint or no linter: request.all() passed to a query, a service or inApp() (WL9005); a POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route with no auth middleware and no public: true (WL9006, the source-side twin of the warlock dev warning, sharing its guard-name rule); a redirect() / navigateTo() / <Link to|href> target read from request input without safeRedirect() / safeRedirectTarget() or an isSafeRedirect() check (WL9007); a raw email, credential or request body in a log call (WL9008, using the logger's default censored keys); a regex with an unbounded quantifier run on request input (WL9009); and, as warnings, await log.*() (WL9010), a second controller in one file (WL9011) and a kind union discriminator (WL9012). A // warlock-check-ignore WL9006 comment on the problem's line or the line above records a deliberate exception. The generated AGENTS.md conventions list and the warlock-conventions skill cover every code.

warlock typecheck [--changed] [--base <ref>] [--project <tsconfig>] [--json] typechecks with the TypeScript compiler API, keeping incremental state in .warlock/cache/typecheck.tsbuildinfo; --changed checks only the changed files and the files importing them.

Stable error codes: a WL + four-digit registry (ERROR_CODES, first digit = area: config, boot, routing, validation, http, database, cli, environment, convention), each with a one-line fix, a skill and a docs anchor, exported from @warlock.js/core and @warlock.js/core/errors with explainErrorCode(), errorCodeOf() (also maps ECONNREFUSED/EADDRINUSE and follows cause) and WarlockError. Framework error classes carry a code (ModuleLoadError → WL2001, ContainerKeyMissingError → WL2004, CliOptionValueError → WL7001, …); a duplicate route name throws RouteNameTakenError (WL3001), and unknown route names, missing URL params, invalid controller actions and refused connector lists throw coded WarlockErrors with unchanged messages. warlock explain <CODE> [--json] prints a code's meaning and fix; warlock explain lists them all.
warlock doctor --json prints the report as JSON, and every warn/fail finding (also in the plain report) carries its error code with the same hint / skill / docs fields warlock check --json uses.

@warlock.js/core/tooling subpath: inspectApp, runCheck, runTypecheck, CHECK_EXIT_CODES and the shared ToolingProblem type, kept off the root barrel because it loads the TypeScript compiler and ESLint.
Skills warlock-inspect and warlock-check; warlock-doctor covers --json and error codes. Docs pages for warlock inspect, warlock check / typecheck and the error-code reference.

warlock make endpoint <module>/<name> (also generate.endpoint / make.endpoint) generates one endpoint from its request schema: --schema (a seal object schema file), --method, --path, --resource, and --auth (default) or --public. It writes the schema module, a service taking validated input, the resource shaped from the schema fields, one controller reading request.validated() with its validation and an OpenAPI responseSchema, the route (in a guarded() block, or marked public: true), the success message in utils/locales.json, and tests/<name>.test.ts, which requests the endpoint over the real HTTP stack with a valid input derived from the schema, a missing required field, and for guarded routes an anonymous 401 plus a signed-in case. Existing files are skipped and reported unless --force; a controller already in routes.ts is not registered twice. warlock make <generator> dispatches to every generator, like warlock generate.

Every generate.* command, make and add accept --dry-run (write nothing; add also installs nothing, running feature setup against an in-memory copy of the files) and --json (one versioned report on stdout listing files written, files skipped because they exist, per-file actions, command details and messages; also printed when the command fails). add --list --json includes the feature catalog.

Test fakes at @warlock.js/core/tests, installed by default in the test environment: mailFake, queueFake, cacheFake, storageFake, clockFake and idsFake, with assertion helpers (assertSent, assertSentCount, assertPushed, assertNotPushed, assertHas, assertStored, assertExists, travel, ...) whose failures list what was recorded. installTestFakes() / restoreTestFakes() and the fakes option of setupTest() / startHttpTestServer() control them; tests.fakes configures them per project. The storage fake's temp root is shared between the HTTP test server and the workers.

clock (now(), timestamp()) and ids (uuid(), token(length)) runtime helpers. Outside tests they are the system clock and node:crypto; in tests the fakes make them deterministic without touching Date or timers.

defineFactory(Model, (seed) => attributes) model factories with make(), makeMany(n), create(), create(n), createMany(n), named states (state() / with()) and a deterministic seed (text, email, uuid, date, number, pick); resetFactorySequences().

createTestHttpServer({ routes?, loadAppModules?, importModule? }) serves requests inside the test worker with the production Fastify setup, plugins and route registration on an OS-assigned port, returning request helpers, actingAs(user) and close(); the worker's fakes see what handlers did. createTestRequestClient(baseUrl) binds the request helpers to any URL, and actingAs(user, client?) accepts one.
startHttpTestServer({ port: 0 }) binds a free port and publishes the bound port to the workers; warlock add test now generates it.
snapshotResponse(response, { redact }) reduces a response to status, content type and body with volatile paths redacted, for toMatchSnapshot().

warlock test [filters...] runs the project's own Vitest with --changed (optionally --since <ref>), --related <files>, --watch, --test-name-pattern and --json; change-scoped runs pass when no test is affected.
Storage exposes isInitialized, driverNames() and getDefaultName(); mail exposes getExplicitMailMode() and resetMailMode().

warlock upgrade --to <version> applies the mechanical edits for each breaking change between the installed release and the target, lists every place that needs a decision with file:line, a hint and the skill to read, and moves every @warlock.js/* dependency to the target. --dry-run prints a unified diff and writes nothing, --json prints the result, --from sets the version upgrading from; without it the command reads the installed @warlock.js/core, which is already the target once the new release is installed, so pass it (warlock upgrade --from 5.30 --to 5.31.0). With no --from and the installed version equal to the target, the command stops and asks for --from <previous version>. Codemods for 5.30 and 5.31: logger-sync-calls, request-log-snapshot, head-viewport, node-22-15, warlock-versions, plus review lists for seal-validate-result, ai-tool-dispatch, ai-anthropic-body, ai-finish-reason, rate-limit-defaults, seal-refine-output, seal-container-catch, seal-union-output and ai-compaction-opt-in. Source edits use ts-morph, an optional peer loaded only by this command; without it the command prints the install command and changes nothing.

Route option public?: boolean (also on router.group(), inherited by its routes; a route's own public: false opts back out) records that a mutating route is intentionally reachable without signing in. It changes nothing at runtime.

warlock dev warns once per route about POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE routes that have no auth middleware and no public: true, listing method, path and route file; HMR-added routes are reported when they commit. Page routes are skipped, production never checks, and http.warnUnguardedRoutes: false turns it off. Middleware counts as a guard when marked with the new markAuthGuard(middleware, isGuard?) (authMiddleware() marks itself) or, unmarked, when its function name contains auth or guard; isAuthGuardMiddleware(), isUnguardedMutatingRoute() and reportUnguardedMutatingRoutes() are exported for tooling.

safeRedirect(target, { allowedOrigins, fallback }) and isSafeRedirect(target, options?): an allowlist for redirect targets taken from request input. Same-origin paths and absolute http(s) URLs on an allowed origin pass; //host, /\host, other schemes, credentials in the URL and control characters fall back to "/" (or fallback). response.redirect() itself is unchanged.

escapeHeaderValue(value) makes any value a valid header value: CR/LF/NUL and other control characters (tab kept) are removed, non-Latin-1 characters become ?, and the result is trimmed, so request input cannot split a header or make Node throw a 500.

Typed, validated configuration: a src/config/<name>.ts file may export configSchema = defineConfigSchema(validator, { env }) next to its default export (ConfigOf<typeof configSchema> types the value). Dev boot, each config hot reload and the production loader warlock build generates validate it before registration and throw one InvalidConfigError listing every problem in every config file (key path, rule message, the environment variable to set), never the values. An invalid config never reaches its special handler; an invalid hot reload keeps the previous value. Files without a schema load as before.

warlock mcp serves the app to coding agents over the Model Context Protocol — stdio by default, or --http (Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1; --token / WARLOCK_MCP_TOKEN required for any other host). Tools: inspect_app and one inspect_<section> per inspect section (with filters, e.g. inspect_routes { unguardedWrites: true }), db_schema (tables, columns, keys and relations from the models), docs_search / docs_read (offline, over the installed @warlock.js/* skills, READMEs and llms files only), explain, check_run, test_run (one file, the tests related to changed files, or the suite), requests_recent (devtools: phases, queries with nPlusOne flags, logs, timings) and generate_make / generate_add, which run the generator in a throw-away copy of the project and return a unified diff. Read-only by default: writing needs --allow-writes, otherwise write: true is refused (WL7005). @warlock.js/ai-tools is a new optional peer, imported only by this command; a missing one fails with WL7003 and the install line. Tool names use _ because model APIs refuse . in tool names.
warlock dev --mcp (or devServer.mcp: true | { port, token, allowWrites }) serves the same tools from the dev server over loopback HTTP, reading the live registries after each hot reload.
warlock dev records its address, devtools mount and MCP endpoint in .warlock/dev-server.json (removed on shutdown); warlock trace and requests_recent read it.

warlock trace <method> <url> [--body json|@file] [--header k:v] [--json] sends one request to the running dev server (correlated by x-request-id) and prints its devtools timeline as a versioned report (schemaVersion: 1): middleware with timings, the validation result and errors, handler time, queries with N+1 flags, logs, cache operations, mails, the response (authorization and cookie headers redacted, bodies capped) and timings. Devtools is checked before anything is sent: WL8008 when the dev server is not running, WL8009 when devtools is not, WL5004 when devtools recorded no timeline; failures exit 2 for this machine and 1 otherwise.

warlock agents-md [--write] [--json] generates the app-specific section of AGENTS.md from the booted app — modules with route and model counts, a routes summary with unguarded writes flagged, models, the conventions warlock check enforces, the installed skills and the verify commands — between <!-- warlock:generated:start --> and <!-- warlock:generated:end -->. Content outside the markers is never changed; malformed markers fail with WL7501 and nothing is written. warlock dev refreshes the section on boot and after reloads (debounced, written only when it changed); devServer.agentsMd: false turns that off.

warlock board init|add|status|send|watch [--json] is a file-based protocol for two coding agents (an implementer and a reviewer) in a git-ignored .warlock/board/: items with the states todo, in-progress, ready-for-review, changes-requested, approved and blocked (refused moves fail with WL7403), append-only numbered messages per recipient (to-<agent>/NNNN-<slug>.md), VERDICT: APPROVED / VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED lines that move the item, and a watch that blocks until a new message arrives or times out (WL7404, exit 3). New codes WL7401–WL7404 cover the board.

runTests({ files | changed | base }) runs the app's vitest for one file, the tests related to changed files, or the suite, with the warlock check problem shape. It and the building blocks of the commands above (startWarlockMcpServer, createMcpContext, createWarlockMcpTools, searchDocs, buildDbSchema, sandboxBackend, applyGeneration, traceRequest, connectDevtools, renderAgentsMdSection, writeAgentsMd, createAgentsMdRefresher, initBoard, watchBoard, …) are exported from @warlock.js/core/tooling.

Skills warlock-mcp, warlock-trace, warlock-agents-md and warlock-board; warlock-inspect points agents at the MCP tools. Docs pages for warlock mcp, warlock trace, warlock agents-md and warlock board, and the new codes on the error-code reference.
End-to-end configuration recipes cover a non-default R2 image disk, variant ingestion and serving, and shared Redis rate-limit windows across two servers with outage behavior.

The upgrade-from-5-29 skill guides application upgrades through logger delivery, tool concurrency, request snapshots, auth counter/lock resets, image cache layouts and viewport metadata. It covers Seal result narrowing and refinement/container/union behavior, AI finish reasons and replay, bounded workspace reads, and production rate-limit migration in 5.31; cut-off AI agent answers (AgentIncompleteError with report.status: "incomplete", continueOnOutputLimit, per-run modelOptions and the Anthropic adapter's larger default max_tokens); the AI cost changes (per-provider cache billing, totalCost, the new built-in model prices and removed defaults, and ProviderOverloadedError); and the AI workspace changes (the larger tools.all() set, the new WorkspaceOps / Workspace methods, nested-command refusals and dispose()).
Skills include complete examples for request cancellation, stream/SSE backpressure and retention, HTTP error mapping, shared rate limits and signed-in test clients.

Notification scaffolds with test support emit real signed-in controller specs and isolated two-recipient fixtures for listing, unread counts, marking one/all read, query validation and ownership checks. Fixtures use the configured auth model and revoke/delete only their own credentials and rows.
actingAs(user) at @warlock.js/core/tests issues a real persisted access token and returns isolated authenticated HTTP helpers. Middleware remains active; client.dispose() revokes only its token.

Optional Oxlint background file checks during development. Install Oxlint in the app and add .oxlintrc.json, .oxlintrc.jsonc, oxlint.config.ts or oxlint.config.mts; changed files are linted in sequential batches in a worker and JSON diagnostics appear with rule, location and severity. Large boot scans stay within platform command-line limits, tool/config failures include actionable CLI output, and results omit source contents. Both configured ESLint and Oxlint run by default; ESLint still needs only its app configuration and uses core's own dependency. devServer.healthCheckers also accepts { typescript?, eslint?, oxlint? } switches while preserving custom arrays and false.

Real Redis integration coverage for cache-backed HTTP rate-limit stores, including concurrent requests, preserved deadlines and counters recreated after a seeded key expires. Local runs opt in with WARLOCK_REDIS_INTEGRATION=1; CI requires a live Redis service. Tests use UUID prefixes and clean only their own keys.

Image variants support object-storage disks through resolveImageVariant, createUploadedFileController and generateImageVariants({ disk, urlPrefix }). Remote originals retain their driver URL; derivatives are cached locally, with bounded source reads and generation keys that isolate buckets and tenant prefixes. ETag metadata avoids downloads on cache hits; sources without an ETag use content hashes. Concurrent downloads are shared, and ingest downloads once for all variants/formats. The default public uploads controller keeps returning 404 for cloud default disks; an explicit disk or remote: true deliberately opts a controller into cloud serving.

uploads.images.maxCacheBytes (default 512 MiB) and maxCacheAge (default seven days) bound cached derivatives. Expired hits render again; cleanup removes expired and oldest files, retaining the derivative being returned even when it alone exceeds the byte budget. Writes schedule a coalesced background sweep at most once per minute; hits never walk the cache and the byte budget is eventual. Idle caches are reclaimed after their next generated derivative.

SSE supports unnamed events (send(undefined, data)) and raw string payloads through a fourth { raw: true } argument, with safe multiline data: encoding. SSE and streams accept explicit cache headers before flushing while protecting protocol/drain headers and keeping safe cache defaults.

SSE and stream controllers gain synchronous enqueue() with a byte cap (maxQueuedBytes, default 1 MiB for enqueue), disconnect/drop overflow policies with a visible dropped counter, ordered draining and flushing accepted queued output on end().

http.logging.private applies path-prefix or regular-expression policies to decoded, normalized request URLs, including unmatched requests. Matching policies check raw, decoded and resolved paths plus the matched route pattern, remove input before snapshots are built and cannot be overridden by per-route logging. Dev-dispatch error URLs use the same policy.

warlock dev exits with code 1 and a clear error when it is started on Bun or Deno: the development server is Node-only. Before, it started partway and then failed in confusing ways. The error names the runtime and points to the production start commands. warlock build on Bun or Deno still runs, but prints a notice that only the Node build is verified.
A source checkout of @warlock.js/core run by a runtime without module.registerHooks now prints what is missing, instead of failing with "registerHooks is not a function".

Static file serving loads @fastify/static on the first file request instead of at boot, including existing public folders and router.directory mounts. The directory globber loads at boot only for wildcard: false. Concurrent first requests share initialization; upstream headers, ranges, listings, decorators and exact routes for wildcard: false are preserved.

Request-log privacy rules (http.logging.private) are prepared once per configured array instead of on every log snapshot: each string prefix is normalised a single time, and a regex rule's need for a fresh copy (global or sticky flags) is decided once. Setting a new array applies its rules; editing the existing array in place is no longer picked up. The logging docs and configure-app skill now also say that a route pattern containing a % that does not decode withholds body and query on every request to that route.

BREAKING: Node.js 22.15 or newer is required (engines.node: ">=22.15"): the warlock CLI loads TypeScript through module.registerHooks, which Node added in 22.15. warlock upgrade --from 5.30 --to 5.31.0 raises the app's engines.node, .nvmrc and .node-version (codemod node-22-15).

Skill examples compile against the current API: the LLM-streaming example iterates agent.stream() events (agent.trip.streaming / event.delta), the raw-query example uses app.database?.driver.query(...), the environment-aware logging example sets per-channel levels (LogConfigurations has no level), the authenticated-test examples use authService.createTokenPair(user) and accessToken.token, devServer.healthCheckers shows a valid value, and examples import or declare everything they use.

Running bin/warlock.js from a source checkout (no esm/ build next to it) no longer crashes every booting command (doctor, inspect, mcp, routes) on Node.js 22.15 with TypeError: t is not a function from dayjs.extend. The bin's TypeScript load hook ran in the main thread, and on 22.15 that hands a CommonJS package the empty, not-yet-run exports of a file an ES module also imports (@mongez/time-wizard requiring the dayjs utc and timezone plugins). The hook now runs in a module.register() loader worker. Bare subpaths of a package consumed as source, such as @warlock.js/core/net, now resolve to the directory's index.ts instead of failing with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT, so warlock mcp loads @warlock.js/ai from source. The published package, which loads compiled output without hooks, was not affected.

Conditional requests follow RFC 9110: If-None-Match uses weak comparison on both sides (a weak current ETag now matches its strong form) and parses quoted tags containing commas; If-Match uses strong comparison, so a W/ tag never satisfies it. response.sendFile(), sendBuffer()/sendImage() with an etag and the uploads variant controller answer a failed If-Match or If-Unmodified-Since with 412, and evaluate the headers in the RFC order.

The development wildcard dispatcher applies the global rate limiter per matched route instead of to every request, so a route exempted with rateLimit: false or serverOptions: { config: { rateLimit: false } }, a static file route and an unmatched URL are not counted, exactly as in production. Routes with a wildcard path share the global bucket in both modes.

warlock generate.module list controllers validate their query (page, limit) with a schema and pass request.validated() to the list service instead of request.all(); the web starter's contact route is registered with public: true.

React module-resolution regressions preserve the ESM package boundary in isolated fixtures and report child-process stderr before checking output, so missing and broken React installations are tested correctly under Node.js 22.15.

The TypeScript worker configured-root regression uses the framework's real source-worker bootstrap on Node.js 22.15, retaining its declaration, update and deletion checks instead of starting an unsupported direct .ts worker entry. The same assertions also run against a built .mjs worker without loader hooks.

Upgrade guidance names AgentConfig.compaction, covers sub-agent dispatch and blank/default validation changes, and explains which routes the production rate quotas cover. In 5.31, purgeImageVariants() preserves legacy two-level cache files; retire them manually, correcting the earlier 5.30 cleanup suggestion.

Per-file image-cache purges refuse symlinked shard directories for local and object-storage disks. Stale-generation pruning now removes only recognized cache files from older generation-shaped folders, preserving current-generation files, unrelated entries, directories and symlinks.
The error-handling guide gives the schema-validation failure status as 422, matching the framework default, and the validation skill's introduction no longer says 400.
The validation skill shows the HTTP 422 body as strict JSON that can be copied into a JSON parser.

Image-variant purges remove only recognized cache files and retain the cache root, directories, unrelated files and symlinks. Purge and background eviction validate every shard/source/generation path component, so a cache nested inside storage cannot recursively delete uploads. Use a dedicated derivative folder.

Notification test fixtures roll back partially created users, tokens and rows on setup failure, attempt all cleanup operations and clear their reference before teardown. actingAs() refuses non-test environments before issuing credentials and revokes a newly issued blank token before rejecting it.

Image-variant generation and purging reject a cache directory that equals or contains any configured local storage root, including runtime-registered disks and symlink aliases. Validation happens in the shared cache-directory resolver, so purgeImageVariants() cannot bypass it and delete uploads through an overlapping cache setting.

Oxlint failures preserve stdout config errors alongside stderr warnings and bound command diagnostics without echoing file arguments. Health-worker shutdown waits briefly for child cleanup before forced termination.
Generator selection prompts reject an empty choices list before opening terminal input; indexed reads retain their validated bounds under stricter compiler checks.

Framework HTTP/2 servers start with default shutdown options and track sessions even without HTTP/1 idle-connection support. Graceful HTTP/2 drains close sessions after active streams finish without setting forbidden connection headers. SSE and stream helpers omit HTTP/1 framing headers on HTTP/2.

Both sse() and stream() ignore caller Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding, Content-Type, Connection, Keep-Alive, Proxy-Connection and Upgrade option headers. HTTP/1.1 retains chunked framing and reusable connections; HTTP/1.0 remains close-delimited without Transfer-Encoding.
Generated Vitest configuration discovers both .test.ts and .spec.ts, including notification controller specs. Existing apps should use include: ["src/app/**/*.{test,spec}.ts"].

Source health-check workers start on Node.js 22.15 through a JavaScript bootstrap and tsx's import API; passing a .ts entry directly to a worker could fail before its loader hook ran. Published .mjs workers keep their direct startup path.
The cache-backed rate limiter supplies its per-window TTL on every atomic increment, so a key that expires after the create-only seed cannot be recreated without an expiry.
The CLI rejects unsupported Node versions with one clear message and a non-zero exit before loading the published entry or registering the source loader.

Image-variant cache sweeps remove writer temporaries left by a crashed write once they are an hour old, and remove a generation's source.json and then its empty directory (after a five-minute grace, never through a symlink) once its derivatives are gone, so object-storage generations no longer pile up when ETags change. Scheduled checks skip the cache walk while the estimate is within budget and nothing has expired; the first check after boot and one per maxCacheAge still walk.

A cache directory or disk root that cannot be resolved (ENOTDIR, EACCES, ELOOP) now throws ImageVariantsConfigError, with the original error as its cause, instead of the raw file-system error. The cache-overlap guard remembers its result per cache, disk root and configured local roots instead of resolving every path on each variant request; a newly registered disk is checked again.

Dev-server Oxlint checks no longer abort a boot scan on one over-long path: it runs in its own batch and, if the OS still refuses it, only that file is reported as unchecked. Batches count each argument's argv pointer on POSIX, hold at most 500 files, and a batch whose report overflows the output buffer is split and retried. Shutdown sends SIGKILL 250 ms after SIGTERM to a CLI child that ignores it, and an interrupted check reports a cancellation instead of a 30-second timeout.

In every release up to and including 5.30.0, the global http.rateLimit did not apply to application routes in production, and per-route rateLimit options had no effect in production (development enforced them). 5.31 enforces both: the shared bucket now covers pages and API routes. Static files (the public folder, router.directory() mounts, router.file() routes and the web build's assets) and the built-in liveness and readiness probes are exempt by default; http.rateLimit.staticFiles: true and http.health.rateLimit: true opt them into the global policy.

Usage.inputIncludesCache says whether input contains the cache counters (set by each first-party adapter; absent reads as true), and Usage.cacheWrite1hTokens counts 1-hour cache writes. Usage merged across providers with different semantics is normalised to true.

ModelPricing.cacheWrite and cacheWrite1h (USD per 1M tokens written to the cache, default and 1-hour lifetime). Cost breakdowns carry cache-write spend in cost.cacheWrite; computeCost also bills reasoningTokens at ModelPricing.reasoning when that rate is set.

totalCost(cost) sums every channel of a cost breakdown; attachCost(usage, pricing) attaches it to a usage. First-party adapters now attach usage.cost to model.complete() and the streaming done chunk when the model is priced, so side calls outside an agent are costed.

ProviderError.status (HTTP status), .billed (true | false | "unknown", failing closed to "unknown" unless the call never reached a billable account or the provider documents the status as free) and .retryable. ProviderErrorOptions and ProviderBilled are exported.
ProviderOverloadedError with code PROVIDER_OVERLOADED (always retryable) for provider overloads; fallbackModel fails over on it by default.

estimateInputTokens(messages, options) — an offline estimate of a call's input tokens (text, tool calls, tool schemas, response schema) — and countInputTokens(model, messages, options), which uses the model's native countTokens when it has one and reports source: "native" | "estimate".

budget({ reserve: { outputTokens, inputTokens? } }): reserve each trip's worst case before the call, commit the actual usage after it, release the reservation when the call fails. Applies to the run caps and, atomically through the store, to scoped ledgers, so concurrent runs cannot jointly overspend. BudgetPricing entries may now be a ModelPricing (cache rates included) besides { inputPer1K, outputPer1K }.

measureTools(tools, { model, mode }) reports the input tokens a tool list adds per call, per tool and in total, counted natively when the model can and estimated otherwise. Registered as ai.tools.measure by @warlock.js/ai-tools.

Compact tool schemas: compactJsonSchema(), extractJsonSchema(schema, { compact }), withCompactJsonSchema(), compactToolSchemas() and the toolSchemas: "full" | "compact" option on ai.agent() and execute(). Compact schemas drop annotations (descriptions, titles, examples, defaults) and collapse const unions to enum; validation is unchanged.
createToolContext({ artifacts?, signal? }) builds the ToolContext for invoking a tool outside the agent loop.

verifyModelSignalContract({ createModel }) checks that a model adapter honours ModelCallOptions.signal: a call with an already-aborted signal rejects, and aborting mid-call rejects promptly and cancels the HTTP request, for complete() and stream(). It serves an ephemeral local port that never answers (protocol: "http2" for HTTP/2 clients), has no test-runner dependency, and throws an Error naming the failed check. Honouring signal is now part of the documented ModelContract, and every first-party adapter runs this check.

continueOnOutputLimit: n on AgentConfig and AgentExecuteOptions: up to n times per run, a response cut off by the output cap is continued with a continue turn and the segments are joined in result.text (and the structured output parsed from it), also on the stream and during repair. A tool call cut off mid-input is dropped and the model is told it did not run. Each continuation is a trip within maxTrips; a full context window is never continued.

agent.execute(input, { modelOptions }) and agent.stream(input, { modelOptions }) set model call options (reasoning effort, maxTokens, cacheControl, providerOptions, …) for that run only, shallow-merged over AgentConfig.modelOptions; the agent is not changed. tools, signal and responseSchema in the per-call object are ignored.

Tool events carry the provider's tool-call id as callId: agent.tool.calling, agent.tool.called and agent.tool.failed (event payloads and stream events), the ToolCall record (report.children[].callId), the tool middleware context (ctx.callId), and the human-approval PolicyContext / ApprovalRequestContext. Concurrent calls to the same tool in one trip can now be told apart. Tool log lines include it.

AgentIncompleteError, AgentIncompleteErrorOptions and AgentIncompleteReason are exported; AIErrorCode gains AGENT_INCOMPLETE, ErrorCategory and ReportStatus gain incomplete, and LLMTrip gains truncatedToolCalls.

agent.stream() emits agent.trip.reasoning (reasoning / thinking text), agent.tool.streaming ({ callId, name, delta } pieces of a tool call's arguments while the model writes them) and agent.trip.usage (running token counts for the trip) wherever the provider streams them. execute() is unchanged; modelOptions.streamChunks turns them down.

ModelStreamChunk gains reasoning, tool-args and usage chunks. They are opt-in on model.stream() through ModelCallOptions.streamChunks (true or { reasoning?, toolArgs?, usage? }), so existing chunk consumers see exactly the old delta / tool-call / done sequence. resolveStreamChunks(options) resolves the option for adapters; MockModel emits all three (scripted reasoning, the tool input as tool-args, a final usage) when asked.

ai.providerTool({ provider, definition, execute? }) declares a provider-defined tool (web search, code execution, bash, text editor, search grounding, …). The agent sends it as ModelCallOptions.providerTools; only the named provider receives the definition, verbatim, and every other adapter skips it with one providerTool.skipped warning. Client-run provider tools dispatch to execute by name. Also exported: isProviderTool, selectProviderTools (adapter helper), ProviderTool, ProviderToolDefinition.
Regression fixtures assert required model and identifier segments before reading them under stricter indexed-access checks; the compiler error budget falls by ten.
Skills include complete examples for per-trip tool concurrency and native token preflight with provider-specific request options.

Agents can opt into automatic history compaction with an explicit token threshold, a summary callback and an optional native/custom counter. System prompts, current input and tool groups are preserved. Applied/skipped decisions are recorded on reports and durable snapshots.

Compaction works on thinking runs. The replaced range always ends before the open tool round, which goes back verbatim with its signed thinking. When kept turns after the range carry signed reasoning, the summary is framed as user context and those turns are marked compaction: "retained" (the summary compaction: "summary"), so adapters whose providers bind reasoning to the exact prior history can leave it out on replay.

ai.compaction.summarize({ model, instructions?, maxTokens?, modelOptions?, onUsage? }) (also summarizeCompaction): a ready-made compaction.summarize callback. It sends the slice as a tagged transcript with Anthropic's published client-side compaction prompt (DEFAULT_COMPACTION_INSTRUCTIONS), reads the <summary> tags, and throws on a truncated, refused or empty reply so the agent keeps the conversation. renderTranscript(messages) is exported for custom callbacks.

ai.session({ id, store, agent, lock? }): a persisted multi-turn conversation with one agent — send, stream, history, load, fork, truncate, resume, clear. Each send stores the whole turn (tool rounds, provider blocks, attachment parts), failed runs leave the history unchanged, sends on one session id are serialized, the agent's compaction policy compacts long sessions, and a send interrupted by a crash resumes through a durable agent.

ai.snapshot.file({ dir }) and ai.snapshot.sqlite({ path } | { database }) snapshot stores for local-first apps, usable for durable runs, supervisor snapshots and sessions. The SQLite store uses Node's built-in node:sqlite (Node 22.5+; no flag on Node 22.13+), loaded only on first use, or any open exec / prepare database such as better-sqlite3; it creates its table on first use unless createTable: false.
Message.compaction / CapturedMessage.compaction ("summary" | "retained"), and a per-call captureMessages option on agent.execute / stream.
ai.snapshot.pg() and ai.snapshot.redis() are generic over the snapshot shape like the other snapshot factories; the default stays SupervisorSnapshot.
ModelContract.countTokens?() represents optional native input-token preflight, separate from offline SDK estimates.
SpawnSubAgentSpec accepts toolDispatch and maxConcurrentTools, forwarded to the fresh agent. Defaults match ai.agent() (concurrent, up to four calls).

ToolContext.request (ToolRequestContext: headers, remoteAddress) carries the inbound request when a server transport runs the tool for a remote client, such as ai.mcp.serve over HTTP. It is unset for in-process dispatch and never reaches the model.

MockModel infers finishReason: "tool_calls" when a scripted response has non-empty toolCalls and no finishReason, so scripted tool calls run without repeating the finish reason. An explicit finishReason still wins.

MockModel honours signal: an already-aborted signal rejects the call, an abort during a scripted delay rejects immediately, and stream() stops between chunks. The rejection is the signal's reason when it is an Error, otherwise an AbortError DOMException.

@warlock.js/ai imports Core's private-address classifier from the new side-effect-free @warlock.js/core/net subpath instead of the Core root, so a standalone process running ai.agent no longer loads Core's HTTP server, database, cache and mail modules, and bundlers no longer need to alias Core. An import-graph test fails if anything reachable from the package entry imports the Core root. The installation guide documents @warlock.js/cache and @warlock.js/cascade as optional, lazily loaded peers for standalone use.

BREAKING An agent run whose final response was cut off — by the output token cap (finishReason: "length") or the context window ("context_exceeded") — no longer finishes as a success with empty or partial text. It ends with result.error an AgentIncompleteError (code: "AGENT_INCOMPLETE", category "incomplete", reason: "output_limit" | "context_window", tripIndex, continuations) and report.status: "incomplete"; result.text keeps the partial text. A tool call the model was still writing is never executed and is listed on the trip's new truncatedToolCalls. Durable snapshots of such a run are stored as failed, so resume() retries the cut-off trip.
The semantic cache never stores a response cut off by the output cap or the context window; a continued answer is stored whole.
The provider matrix documents inherited providerOptions.openai.body on xAI, Groq, DeepSeek and Mistral, and warns against sharing provider-specific fields across incompatible fallback models.

Skill examples compile against the current API: the guardrail skills import from @warlock.js/ai (guardrails ship in core; there is no @warlock.js/ai-guard package), ai.config({ defaultStore }) awaits cache.driver(...), MockSDK is called without new, the observer skill no longer lists the internal clearObservers, the vector-store tool maps { key, score, value } hits, and examples declare the agents, tools and clients they use.

computeCost bills Anthropic and Bedrock prompt caching correctly. Their input excludes cache reads and writes, so cache reads are no longer subtracted from it (which could floor fresh input at 0), and cache writes are now charged: at ModelPricing.cacheWrite, with the 1-hour share at cacheWrite1h. OpenAI-style usage, where input includes cached tokens, is billed as before.
Batch, planner and fallback-model usage rollups use the shared mergeUsage, so they keep every usage channel and the cache semantics flag.

The streaming agent loop reads the finish reason and usage only from the done chunk and ignores chunk types it does not know, instead of treating any other chunk as done. fallbackModel().stream() still falls over after a model emitted only a usage chunk.

Automatic compaction preserves the original execution input during output repair and durable resume, records its updated snapshot index, and frames a first-turn summary as user context. Legacy snapshots with missing or ambiguous input skip compaction safely.

A durable snapshot's persisted input index is trusted on resume only when it is an integer inside the conversation that points at a user message. An out-of-range, negative, fractional or non-user index (a corrupted or hand-edited snapshot) falls back to finding the unique matching input, and compaction itself refuses to protect a non-user message, recording no-safe-range instead of summarising the input.

First release: drive vendor coding-agent CLIs headless as agents. cli.<vendor>(options) (also ai.cli.<vendor> after importing the package) returns a CLI agent. run(prompt, { cwd, resume, signal, timeoutMs, model, effort, permission, mcp, env, apiKey, args }) starts one session, and returns CliSession with events, done() and cancel().

Adapters for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Cursor, Copilot, Grok Build, OpenCode, Amp, Factory Droid, Mistral Vibe, Aider and Reasonix. Each records the CLI version, the official sources, and whether it was verified against the real --help or against the docs (adapter.verification).

One event model for every vendor: session.started, message (deltas and complete messages), tool.call, tool.result, usage, error and session.ended. session.done() resolves { status, text, messages, usage, sessionRef, exitCode, signal, error, stderr, durationMs } and never rejects.

Capability probe: before the first run, the CLI's --version and help screens are read, and every flag the launch plan relies on must be listed. A missing flag fails the run with CliError (type: "capability"), naming the flag and the installed version.

Secrets never go to argv: - API keys travel in the environment (apiKey). - Per-run MCP servers are written as a mode-0600 file in a private per-run directory, removed after the run. - Each run gets a private config home by default (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, COPILOT_HOME, GROK_HOME, …). home also takes a path you own, or "inherit".
permission defaults to "standard", the CLI's own non-interactive approval rules. Each vendor's approve-everything mode is used only with permission: "bypass".

Windows spawn rules: - PATHEXT lookup. - npm and pnpm .cmd shims are unwrapped to node <script> (or their native .exe). - Other batch files fall back to cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /c with every argument quoted, refusing bytes cmd.exe cannot carry. - The prompt moves to stdin or a prompt file when argv cannot carry it.
Cancellation (signal, cancel()) and timeoutMs kill the CLI's whole process tree. On POSIX this is its own process group, with SIGTERM then SIGKILL; on Windows, taskkill /T /F on its PID.
agent.model(config) / cliModel(agent, config) wraps a CLI agent as a ModelContract, so ai.agent and its budget, guardrail, observer and fallback middleware can drive a CLI.

createCliAgent(adapter, options) / cli.custom(adapter) and the documented CliAdapter interface let apps add vendors. The building blocks are exported: jsonLinesParser, createClaudeStreamParser, mcpServersJson, toToml, mapEffort, requirePrivateHome and more.

session.cancel(), or aborting the run's signal, after the run has finished no longer signals the CLI's old process group. Once the CLI's pipes close, cancellation is a no-op, so a finally { session.cancel() } cannot reach an unrelated process that reused the pid. The abort listener is also removed when the run settles.

Skills include complete examples for viewport metadata, typed Link wrappers, runtime route-name checks and independent form submissions with query parameters. Settled-outcome guidance handles action errors and dropped submissions separately from completed requests.
Development checks compile the optional Web Vitals example against its actual types; Web Vitals remains an app-installed optional dependency.

<Form onSettled={outcome => …}> observes every enhanced submission outcome, including network failures and dropped submissions, after the existing success/error callbacks. Native browser submissions do not invoke it.
A submit button marked data-independent opts that submission into independent mode, so a Cancel button can run beside Start within the same form.

Sitemap routes compare If-Match strongly and answer 412 when it does not name the exact strong ETag; If-None-Match keeps weak comparison and both use core's RFC 9110 precondition evaluation. The W/ weakness prefix is matched case-sensitively, as the RFC defines it.

Pages render on Bun and Deno. Both runtimes resolve a bare react-dom/server import through their own export conditions to a React build without renderToPipeableStream, so every page request on a built app failed with "renderToPipeableStream is not a function" (HTTP 500). The page renderer now loads React's Node server build, react-dom/server.node, when the selected build cannot stream. Node keeps the module it selected before.

The server-page-cache test fixture explicitly disables unrelated HTTP throttling and restores its previous configuration on teardown, so repeated cache requests exercise cache behavior after production rate-limit enforcement was corrected.

Published page skills include complete support modules, schemas and generated-type prerequisites; their HTTP examples and Vitest discovery match current APIs. The skill compile gate verifies them without a failure allowance.
The root middleware example declares its own request-local type rather than depending on another skill's augmentation.

Guarded useUser(name) retains the last committed signed-in user when a concurrent transition suspends and is abandoned. Navigation callbacks also read the committed page, and boundary reset counters commit with their page swap. A regression verifies that an abandoned transition preserves the visible error fallback and does not report its error again before the next committed swap.

Locale context reuse after development edits is covered by a real Vite dev-server/HMR regression: a retained provider continues to serve refreshed locale and translation hooks after repeated filesystem edits. An unshared-context control reproduces the missing-provider HTTP failure.

<Form>'s onSettled documentation says that a form unmounting drops only independent submissions (the form's independent prop or a data-independent submit button); other in-flight submissions are not aborted by an unmount. Regression tests cover onSettled running once when onSuccess throws and a data-independent button's submission being aborted on unmount.

The global HTTP rate limiter that 5.31 enforces covers page routes and API routes; the production client bundle (/assets/*) and the public files copied by warlock build are static files and exempt by default, so one page load's script, stylesheet, font and image requests do not spend the visitor's quota. http.rateLimit.staticFiles: true counts them again. In development, Vite answers module and asset requests before any route runs, so they never count.

Built-in Claude API list prices (ANTHROPIC_MODEL_PRICING, anthropicPricingFor, withAnthropicCacheWriteRates), from Anthropic's pricing page as of 2026-10-17, used when neither the model nor the SDK registry is priced. Dated snapshot ids resolve to their alias. Claude Haiku 5.5 (priced by prompt length) is left unpriced.
complete() and the streaming done chunk attach usage.cost when the model is priced.
529 / overloaded_error responses and mid-stream overload events throw ProviderOverloadedError; every wrapped error carries status, billed and retryable.
An adapter contract test verifies that aborting signal rejects complete() and stream() on the model and cancels the HTTP request.
AnthropicModelConfig.maxOutputTokens overrides the inferred model output limit that sizes the default max_tokens.

With streamChunks, stream() yields reasoning for thinking_delta, tool-args for the input_json_delta of client tool_use blocks, and usage after message_start and each message_delta. send() takes the same streamChunks transport option.

ai.providerTool({ provider: "anthropic", definition }) entries (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution, bash, text_editor, memory, …) are sent verbatim ahead of the function tools; the prompt-cache breakpoint stays on the last function tool. Other providers' tools are skipped with a warning. The reserved providerOptions.anthropic.body keys are unchanged.

Typed context management on providerOptions.anthropic: contextManagement.clearToolUses / clearThinking (clear_tool_uses_20250919 / clear_thinking_20251015, beta context-management-2025-06-27) and serverCompaction (compact_20260112, beta compact-2026-01-12, trigger of at least 50,000 input tokens). The adapter builds the edits in the order the API requires and adds the beta headers; combining them with body.context_management fails with InvalidRequestError.
thinkingBlockBinding: "error" | "drop_block" sends thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior with the thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 beta.

Preserved thinking after client-side compaction: on Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 an assistant turn marked compaction: "retained" is replayed without its thinking blocks, which were produced against the replaced history. AnthropicModelConfig.preservedThinking overrides the inference; inferPreservedThinking(name) and ToAnthropicMessagesOptions are exported.
AnthropicModel.buildRequest() creates a detached request snapshot for preflight auditing; send(request) sends that snapshot as a completion or stream without rebuilding its body.
Message, tool and provider-block converters and request types are exported from the package root for hosts using their own transport.

reasoning: { effort: "none" } now turns thinking off on Claude Sonnet 5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 with thinking: { type: "disabled" } (sent alone, so Haiku 5.5 stays at its default effort, inside the range where disabled is accepted). Previously no thinking field was sent and both models ran adaptive thinking by default.

reasoning: { effort: "none" } on Claude Opus 5 now sends adaptive thinking at output_config.effort: "low" instead of omitting thinking (which ran at the default high). Opus 5 is deliberately not sent disabled: with thinking off it can write a tool call as plain text that never runs, and leak thinking tags. Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5 / 5.1 are unchanged.

BREAKING The default max_tokens (when no maxTokens is set) rose from 4096. Streaming requests use the model's documented max output — 128K for the Claude 5 family and Opus 4.6–4.8 / Sonnet 4.6, 64K for Opus / Sonnet / Haiku 4.5 — and non-streaming requests use 16384, capped by the model's max output (the Anthropic SDK requires streaming for larger non-streaming requests unless the client sets a timeout). Unknown ids default to 16384. With thinking on, the default still keeps room for the thinking budget plus 4096 answer tokens, within the model's limit.

Usage is marked inputIncludesCache: false (Anthropic's input_tokens excludes cache reads and writes), and 1-hour cache writes are reported in cacheWrite1hTokens from cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens — or, when the breakdown is missing, from a request whose every cache marker asked for ttl: "1h". Cost now bills reads and writes once each, at their own rates.
Caller pricing that omits cache-write rates gets Anthropic's documented multipliers (5-minute writes 1.25x input, 1-hour writes 2x) instead of billing writes at nothing.

Usage includes server-side compaction: the compaction entries of usage.iterations, which the top-level token counts leave out, are added to input, output and the cache counts (completions and streams).
complete() always builds a non-streaming request, including when an indexed stream option is supplied.

A request that fails to build in complete(), stream() or countTokens() (a reserved providerOptions.anthropic.body key, or a body value structuredClone cannot copy, such as a function) is logged like a send failure and rejects with an AIError; errors that are not already one become an InvalidRequestError carrying the original as cause. Before, the raw error escaped unlogged. buildRequest() itself still throws the raw error.
The debug log line for a streaming request reads "Starting streaming call to messages.create" again; non-streaming requests keep "Starting call to messages.create".
The provider docs and setup-anthropic skill say that send() passes betas only to the "beta.messages" endpoint.

list_dir tool and ws.listDir(path, { depth, ignore }): a bounded, jailed directory listing (breadth-first, types and file sizes, denyPaths and list.ignore left out, symlinks reported but never followed), configured by the new list policy (ignore, maxDepth, maxEntries).

multi_edit tool and ws.multiEdit({ path, edits, expectHash }): several exact-string replacements in one file, applied in order and written once — all of them or none. WorkspaceEditError.editIndex names the failing edit.

Background commands: with shell.background ({ maxJobs?, timeoutMs? }), run_shell({ background: true }) / ws.startShell() start a long-running command owned by the workspace; shell_output / ws.shellOutput(id, { since, waitMs }) read its new output (newest shell.maxOutputBytes kept, with a cursor), and shell_kill / ws.shellKill(id) kill its whole process tree. ws.listShells() lists them; WorkspaceJobError reports an unknown id. Backends implement the new optional start().
ws.dispose() kills every background command (whole process trees) and makes the workspace refuse new commands; trees still running when the Node process exits are killed too.
todo_write / todo_read tools and ws.writeTodos() / ws.readTodos(): an in-memory todo list per workspace, shared with its readonly() / scope() projections. TodoStore is exported.

shell.denyPatterns (string prefix patterns or RegExps) and shell.allowCommand(argv, ctx) (return true, false, or a refusal explanation) check every command's arguments, so a policy can refuse git push --force or rm -rf / while allowing git and rm.

shell.interpreter: "sh" — an explicit opt-in to shell syntax. The line runs through /bin/sh -c (cmd.exe /d /v:off /s /c on Windows) after it is parsed and every simple command in it — inside ;, &&, ||, pipes, subshells, $( ), backticks, here-documents and NAME=value prefixes — is checked against deny / allow / denyPatterns / allowCommand. Redirection targets and cd directories must stay in the jail (re-checked with symlinks resolved). Syntax the parser cannot read with confidence is refused. The default stays "none" (argv, no shell).

WorkspacePolicyError.reason (WorkspaceShellRefusalReason: "metacharacter", "unbalanced-quotes", "denied-executable", "not-allowed", "denied-pattern", "nested-command", "unsupported-syntax", "path-escape") and executable, so hosts can phrase refusals themselves. In argv mode the message suggests the split, e.g. "&& is not supported in argv mode: run git add -A, then git commit -m …, as separate commands."
checkShellCommand(policy, command) returns the shell policy's verdict (reason, message, every checked argv, paths) without running anything; analyzeArgvCommand() and tokenizeCommand() are exported.
Backends may implement an optional stat(); the local and mock backends do. The mock backend's scripted commands accept running: true for background starts.
The workspace skill and docs cover the new tools, shell mode, argument rules, background commands and dispose().

The docs, the skill and the path resolver's comments explain how the workspace jail differs from @warlock.js/fs's new confined reader (fs.confined) and why the workspace keeps its own resolver: it accepts absolute paths inside the jail, allowPaths roots, denyPaths, links that stay inside and paths that do not exist yet. Behaviour is unchanged.
The package README no longer ends with a stray empty code block.
The workspace tools now publish a JSON Schema of their input, so providers send the model the real parameter names instead of an empty object schema.
run_tests quotes its pattern for the shell in use: single quotes under interpreter: "sh", so $ and backticks in a test-name filter stay literal.

Wrapper commands no longer hide the command they run: env, time, timeout, nice, nohup, command, builtin, exec and find -exec are unwrapped and the inner command is checked too, and a wrapper used with options the policy cannot read is refused. Before, env rm -rf / passed a deny: ["rm"] policy.
shell.deny matches executable names case-insensitively, so RM on a case-insensitive filesystem no longer slips past deny: ["rm"].
A model-supplied timeoutMs on run_shell can now only lower shell.timeoutMs, as documented, never raise it.

Shell mode removes ENV, BASH_ENV, SHELLOPTS, BASHOPTS, CDPATH, IFS, PS4, GLOBIGNORE and BASH_FUNC_* from the spawned environment, refuses assignments to such variables, refuses & (use background commands), and refuses arithmetic-evaluating constructs ($(( )), array subscripts in builtins) that bash can use to run hidden commands.

The docs, README and skill now state plainly that shell mode is a policy layer checked before /bin/sh runs the line (defence in depth), not an OS sandbox, and recommend running untrusted agents in a container, microVM or as a separate unprivileged user.
Killing a background command, a timeout and dispose() signal only the process tree the workspace spawned (its own process group on POSIX, taskkill /T on its PID on Windows).

ai.mcp(server, { signal }) binds the client to a run: when the signal aborts the client closes its transport, and later handshakes and tool calls fail with an McpTransportError of type "closed". Every tools/call honors both the client signal and the per-call ctx.signal.
ai.tools.measure(tools, { model, mode }) — the measureTools helper from @warlock.js/ai — measures the input tokens a tool list costs per call.

ai.mcp.serve(source, { transport: { type: "http" } }) serves the MCP Streamable HTTP transport on node:http (no extra dependency). It binds 127.0.0.1 on a free port at /mcp by default (host, port, path override them), and start() resolves { url, close }. close() stops accepting connections, waits up to drainTimeoutMs (default 5 s) for in-flight calls, then aborts their ctx.signal and frees the port. The endpoint is stateless: JSON responses, 202 for notifications, 405 for GET / DELETE, 400 for batches or an unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version.
HTTP auth: auth: { bearer } accepts one token or a rotation list; auth: { authorize(request) } runs a custom check; with both set, a request must pass both. Failures get 401 before the body is read.
Tools served over HTTP receive the inbound request on ctx.request (headers, remoteAddress), for per-user tokens, tenant headers or trace ids.
Grouped sources: serve({ groups: { name: tools } }, { prefixToolNames: true }) exposes <group>_<tool>; a function builds custom names.
Optional MCP resources (resources: [{ uri, name, read }]) and prompts (prompts: [{ name, arguments, get }]), with their capabilities advertised only when configured. The server also answers ping.

McpServeError (type: "collision", "config", "listen"), SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, and the McpHttpServeTransport, McpHttpAuth, McpHttpRequestInfo, McpServeHandle, McpHttpServeHandle, McpServeResource, McpServePrompt, McpServeCallContext, McpToolSource, McpGroupedToolSource types. createServeHandler(...).handle(request, context?) takes an optional call context.

initialize negotiates the protocol version: a client's requested version is echoed when supported (2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26), otherwise the newest is offered. It previously always answered 2025-06-18.
McpServer.start() resolves a handle ({ url?, close }) instead of void. The http transport's port is optional.

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk is no longer listed as an optional peer dependency. The MCP client never imported it: it speaks MCP's JSON-RPC itself over a child process (stdio) and fetch (http). The SDK is now a development dependency, used only by the interoperability test against the official client. The MCP docs, README and connect-mcp-server skill now say so, and name ajv as the client's only optional peer.

The stdio transport of ai.mcp.serve() no longer crashes the process when a line is JSON but not a request object (null, a number, an array): it answers a JSON-RPC "Invalid Request" error (-32600, id: null). A failure while answering a line is answered as an internal error and can no longer become an unhandled rejection.
The HTTP transport binds loopback by default and refuses to start on any non-loopback host without auth (McpServeError, type: "config").

Bearer tokens are compared with crypto.timingSafeEqual over SHA-256 digests, so neither content nor length leaks through timing; every configured token is checked. Empty tokens are refused, and an authorize hook that throws denies the request.

Origin is validated on every request, per the MCP transport's DNS-rebinding guidance: loopback origins and allowedOrigins pass, others (including null) get 403. While bound to loopback, a Host header other than localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1] or allowedHosts also gets 403.
Request bodies over maxBodyBytes (default 1 MiB) get 413 and the connection is closed.

With a cacheControl breakpoint, a cachePoint is also placed after the system prompt and, for Claude, after the tool definitions — the prefix segments Bedrock caches in tools → system → messages order. ttl: "1h" (per call, or the new promptCacheTtl model option) is sent only to models that accept it.

Built-in Claude prices for global. and us. inference profiles (BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING, BEDROCK_US_PRICING, bedrockPricingFor), from AWS's Bedrock price list as of 2026-10-17; caller pricing for Claude models gets the 1.25x / 2x cache-write rates filled (withClaudeCacheWriteRates). complete() and the streaming done chunk attach usage.cost when priced.
Claude 5 families and Nova 2 Lite are recognised as prompt-caching capable.
ServiceUnavailableException throws ProviderOverloadedError; wrapped errors carry status, billed and retryable.

new BedrockSDK({ apiKey, region }) authenticates with an Amazon Bedrock API key: requests carry Authorization: Bearer <apiKey> instead of a SigV4 signature and the AWS credential chain is not consulted (the adapter sets the AWS SDK's token and authSchemePreference: ["httpBearerAuth"]). An empty key, or a key combined with credentials or token, throws InvalidRequestError.
An adapter contract test verifies that aborting signal rejects complete() and stream() and cancels the HTTP/2 request.
With streamChunks, stream() yields reasoning for reasoningContent.text deltas and tool-args for client toolUse.input deltas.
ai.providerTool({ provider: "bedrock", definition }) appends a Converse Tool member such as { systemTool: { name: "nova_grounding" } } verbatim; other providers' tools are skipped with a warning.
providerOptions.bedrock.body forwards native per-call request options for completions and streams while protecting the model, conversation and tool definitions.
Models expose native countTokens() preflight using the generation request's Converse conversation, tools and additional model fields.

Provider body objects replace the adapter-built object when their string type discriminator changes, so format and tool-choice overrides do not retain incompatible fields from the old variant. Same-type and undiscriminated objects keep the one-level merge.

A failed rule result may carry errors: [{ error, path }] to report several errors, each at its own path, under the rule's type.
Successful custom rules may return a data property to replace the current validated value, including explicit undefined; omitting the property preserves the value.

Object factories return their already typed class directly, avoiding a duplicate Standard Schema intersection and reducing compiler work for composed schemas. CI now checks the Seal inference benchmark against its updated baseline.

v.union(...) tries every member whose type matches before failing, so a union of several object schemas accepts a value that matches a later member; firstErrorOnly limits the errors reported, not the members tried. A failing union reports its closest member: fewest mismatched literals, then fewest errors, then the deepest error path, then declaration order.
A failing union no longer stores its last member error on the shared rule, so a later validation with no type-matching member reports the default message instead of a stale one.
The custom-error locale example is strict JSON, with its filename outside the code fence.
Standalone string replacement mutators accept an omitted context or options and preserve the stringified input instead of throwing.
Object .merge() retains refinements from both schemas, in their original order; cloning, extending and selecting fields preserve the original schema's refinements.
Union and record Standard Schema types now distinguish child input from validated output; Infer.Output reads the Standard Schema output parameter. Defaults and catches remain guaranteed in output.
Object, array, tuple and lazy Standard Schema output declarations preserve child defaults and catches independently of their input types.

v.tuple([...]) infers one type per position: v.tuple([v.string(), v.int()]) is typed [string, number] for input and output instead of (string | number)[], so a value with swapped positions no longer type-checks. A BaseValidator[] variable is still accepted.

Consecutive messages that map to the same Gemini role are sent as one content with their parts in order. The results of parallel tool calls now travel as a single user turn of functionResponse parts in call order instead of one turn per result, and an agent compaction summary next to a same-role turn merges into it, so requests keep alternating user and model turns. Each functionCall keeps its own thoughtSignature, and countTokens() counts the same contents.

FileLog fileName option: a pattern ("app-{YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}", tokens {YYYY} {MM} {DD} {HH} {mm} {name} in local time) or a (date) => string function, evaluated at every write; it replaces the chunk's default name. rotateFileName takes the same forms and is rendered at each rotation (a getter passed in the config was read once, at construction, so every archive kept the boot date). Exported FileNameOption, FileLogRetention, DAILY_FILE_NAME, HOURLY_FILE_NAME and ROTATE_FILE_NAME.

FileLog retention: { maxFiles?, maxAgeDays?, match? }: removes old log files on boot and whenever the channel starts a new file (a size rotation or a dated name rolling over), plus channel.prune() on demand. It only considers files in the log directory (each group directory with groupBy) whose names match the channel's file name pattern, keeps the file being written, and reports failures to onChannelError instead of throwing. A function fileName needs retention.match. Invalid maxFiles/maxAgeDays throw a TypeError at construction.

LogChannel.reportError(error, entry) and setErrorReporter(reporter) (type ChannelErrorReporter): a channel reports failures outside log() to the onChannelError handler of the logger it was added to (addChannel, setChannels, configure({ channels })), or one stderr line without one.

escapeLogValue(value, { maxLength? }) makes client-controlled text safe inside a log line: CR/LF/tab become visible \r/\n/\t, other control characters (NUL, DEL, C1, U+2028/U+2029) become \uXXXX, ANSI escape sequences are removed, and maxLength cuts with a …[truncated] marker. A user agent or form field can no longer forge entries in console or file logs.
Skills demonstrate email masking inside text, channel-error observation and bounded asynchronous log drains.
With groupBy, size rotation renames the group file that grew too large instead of the ungrouped top-level file.

A file name that throws while a buffer is written (a fileName function, or an overridden fileName getter) is reported as a failed write instead of leaving the channel stuck in its writing state; later writes go through.
