authMiddleware() marks itself as an auth guard (markAuthGuard() from @warlock.js/core), so warlock dev's unguarded-route warning recognises routes behind it; the { optional: true } form is marked as not a guard. Docs and skills list what throttles auth endpoints by default (core's global limit, plus the throttles new apps attach to sign-in and password recovery) and how to add them to an existing app.

Real Redis integration coverage for login failure counters and lockouts, including concurrent requests, preserved deadlines and counters recreated after a seeded key expires. Local runs opt in with WARLOCK_REDIS_INTEGRATION=1; CI requires a live Redis service. Tests use UUID prefixes and clean only their own keys.

Login, token and OTP throttles pass their counting-window TTL into each atomic increment. A counter that expires between the create-only seed and increment is recreated with an expiry rather than becoming permanent. Token middleware regression assertions cover the issue counters' one-hour window and the consume counter's fifteen-minute window.

fs.confined(root, options) / createConfinedReader(root, options): a reader confined to one folder, for folders you do not control (a user-chosen import folder, an extracted upload). readText, readBuffer, readJson (optional Standard Schema), stat, exists, list and walk (async, depth-first) take root-relative paths. The root is canonicalised once and refused when it is itself a symlink (unless allowSymlinkedRoot); absolute paths and .. that climb above the root throw FsPathEscapeError; every path component is checked with lstat and a symlink or Windows junction anywhere throws FsLinkRefusedError; files are opened with O_NOFOLLOW where available and the opened handle's device/inode must match the checked entry, so a file or parent folder swapped between check and open is refused. maxFileBytes (default 16 MiB) is enforced while reading, maxEntries (default 100 000) and maxDepth (default 64) bound list/walk, with FsLimitExceededError. followLinks: true follows only links whose target stays inside the root.

FsPathEscapeError, FsLinkRefusedError, FsLimitExceededError (each with a type discriminator, path and the reason or limit), the ConfinedReader / ConfinedEntry / ConfinedStats types, and isPathInside(child, root).

Clarify the concurrency contract of moveDirectoryNoReplaceAsync / fs.dirs.moveNoReplace at the call-site documentation: the exclusive destination claim protects cooperating writers, while an empty placeholder swapped before its first identity read or after its last check can still be replaced. expectedSource and syncParents do not eliminate those windows. Deterministic interleaving tests preserve these documented limits.
registeredJobs() and queueOf() are exported, so tools can list the jobs an app defined with defineJob() and the queue each runs on; warlock inspect reads them for its jobs section.

setDispatchInterceptor({ dispatch, find? }) / getDispatchInterceptor(): while an interceptor is set, every job's dispatch() and find() go to it instead of BullMQ, so nothing connects to Redis. The slot is process-wide. queueFake in @warlock.js/core/tests is built on it.
Local Redis integration tests skip with a clear service message when Redis is unavailable; CI and explicitly requested integration runs fail instead. Unit cases remain runnable without Redis.

Real Redis integration coverage for atomic counters and their expiry behavior, including concurrent requests, preserved deadlines and counters recreated after a seeded key expires. Local runs opt in with WARLOCK_REDIS_INTEGRATION=1; CI requires a live Redis service. Tests use UUID prefixes and clean only their own keys.

cache.increment(key, amount, { ttl }) supplies a TTL when an atomic increment creates or recreates a counter, through direct, tagged and scoped calls. Existing expiry deadlines are preserved; an explicit TTL also repairs a live permanent counter across drivers. Redis applies the count and TTL together, so an expired seed cannot leave a permanent counter even when the driver has no default TTL.
Access skills no longer end in stray code fences, and the cache configuration recipe is an object expression rather than a labelled statement.
The model-events skill uses Model.globalEvents().on() for global listeners; the abstract base model's per-model on() shortcut requires a concrete subclass.

The devtools-overview skill shows how to read a request's devtools timeline from the terminal with warlock trace, and how coding agents read recent requests through the requests_recent tool of warlock mcp. The JSON API they use (GET <path>/api/requests, GET <path>/api/requests/:id) is unchanged.
Local Redis integration tests skip with a clear service message when Redis is unavailable; CI and explicitly requested integration runs fail instead. Unit cases remain runnable without Redis.

releases.summaryHtml: Fixes for issues found while building real apps on 5.29, plus a security and correctness review. Security: request logs no longer carry OAuth codes, signed-URL credentials or raw Request/Response objects (route logging policy, masked URLs and query), log and cache output masks email addresses with a linear pattern, <Form> only enhances same-origin targets and redirects refuse javascript: targets on the server and the client, SSE event names and ids are stripped of line breaks, login throttles key by an HMAC of the credential, and parallel AI tool calls are capped and serialised per file. HTTP: a request-lifetime request.signal, bounded SSE and stream retention with backpressure, graceful shutdown that closes idle keep-alive connections, typed http.serverOptions, http.errorMapper, shared rate limits through @warlock.js/cache, and @warlock.js/core/errors. Seal: v.literal("") and .default("") keep empty strings, optional discriminated unions accept omitted fields, and validate() returns typed output. Web: 4xx error pages hydrate, <Head /> renders the viewport, <Form independent>, redirect submissions wait for the new page, and production starts without Vite or Babel. Breaking: log methods return the logger instead of a promise (await log.flush() waits), and AI tool calls in one trip run concurrently by default (toolDispatch: "sequential"). create-warlock works on pnpm 9 and 10 again. Lockstep release across all 31 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.30.0 tarballs passed the release gate; after publishing, the registry confirm timed out on a delayed @warlock.js/ai-mistral publish, every package was then confirmed at npm origin and the family installed from npm, and the blog check against npm was not run in that job.

items.html: request.signal: an AbortSignal that aborts when the client disconnects before the response finishes (not when the request body finishes reading, never on normal completion); its listener is attached on first access and removed when the response closes.

Stream backpressure: response.stream()'s controller gains write(data) (sends, then waits until the client can take more; false once it is gone), drain(), backpressured, signal (aborted on client disconnect, not on end()) and onDisconnect(fn), matching response.sse().
SSE backpressure: sse.write(event, data, id?) sends and waits until the client can take more (false once it is gone), plus sse.drain(), sse.backpressured and sse.signal (aborted on disconnect).

http.serverOptions is typed (HttpServerOptions), including Node's native http options such as serverOptions.http.maxHeaderSize; it was already forwarded to Fastify but the config type could not express it.

@warlock.js/core/errors: a side-effect-free subpath with HttpError and its subclasses (BadRequestError, ResourceNotFoundError, …). A standalone helper or worker can import it without bundling Cascade, Cache or the MongoDB driver; the classes are the same ones the root exports, so instanceof holds across both.

http.errorMapper: map errors that are not an HttpError to { status, message?, payload? } (or an HttpError), so domain errors shared with non-HTTP processes need not extend Core. A mapped 5xx stays opaque unless the mapper sets a message; a mapper that throws is logged and ignored.

Per-route request logging policy: logging: { body?: boolean, query?: boolean } on a route, with app-wide defaults under http.logging (plus redactQueryParams). It is applied before any log entry is built, so a schema- or middleware-rejected body never reaches a log channel.
request.toLogSnapshot(), buildRequestLogSnapshot() and redactUrlCredentials(): the bounded, plain-data view of a request that log entries now carry.
purgeImageVariants(path?, { disk? }) removes one file's cached image derivatives, or a disk's whole derivative cache.

createUploadedFileController({ disk }) serves the originals and variants of any local disk, and resolveImageVariant({ disk?, path, variant, format? }) resolves (and renders on a miss) one variant for an app's own route, e.g. a private disk behind auth. uploadedFileController is createUploadedFileController().

Shared rate limits: http.rateLimit.store: "cache" counts in @warlock.js/cache, so every process on a shared driver (Redis, Postgres) shares the limit; middleware.rateLimit() follows it or takes its own store and a stable name. A @fastify/rate-limit store class can be passed as store too. Windows are fixed and clock-aligned. Each route with its own rateLimit counts separately (namespaced by method and URL from the plugin's routeInfo, hashed so /users/:id and /users/id never merge). A cache outage fails open on both limiters (skipOnError defaults to true for this store) and is logged at most once a minute. The null and file cache drivers are refused with UnsupportedRateLimitDriverError (one stores nothing, the other never sweeps expired windows and does not share increments between processes).

response.stream() no longer keeps rendered chunks. response.body after end() holds the last retainChunks chunks written by send(), write() or render() (response.stream(type, { retainChunks }), default 0); it used to hold every render() chunk.
response.stream(): after the client disconnects, send()/render() are silent no-ops and ended is true (they used to write to the closed socket); send() after end() still throws.

@fastify/static is only loaded when there is something to serve — at least one router.directory(), or an existing public folder (storage.publicRoot, which now also accepts false to turn it off). Its directory-listing module calls os.cpus() at load, which cost a measured ~0.4–0.5 s of cold start in an app that served neither. With no public folder, reply.sendFile is no longer decorated by that plugin; response.sendFile() is unaffected.
@warlock.js/core/errors also resolves inside the framework repository (a root errors/index.ts re-export, not published), so workspace packages and tests can import it by its package name.

response.sse() no longer keeps every sent event. response.body after end() holds the last retainEvents events (response.sse({ retainEvents }), default 0), so long-lived streams no longer grow with their history.

BREAKING (only for a custom log channel that reads context.request/context.response): request log entries carry a RequestLogSnapshot, not the Request/Response instances (context.request is { id, method, url, route, name, ip, userAgent, query?, body? }; response.log adds { statusCode }). Native request/reply graphs no longer reach log channels, and credential-bearing query values (secret, token, apiKey, signature, code, X-Amz-*, …) are masked in the logged URL. warlock upgrade --from 5.29 --to 5.31.0 applies the mechanical part (codemod request-log-snapshot).

warlock add notifications writes a smaller, convention-following module: models/notification/ (model with a NotificationResource, migration), resources/, a validated schema/list-notifications.schema.ts (limit capped at 50, no request.all()), a guarded types/notifications-request.type.ts, services/, utils/locales.json, one controller per file for list / unread-count / mark-read / mark-all-read registered through router.route(), a commented gate() permission hook, and a 401 spec per controller when the app has the test feature. The clear-all and delete endpoints are no longer generated. Apps that already have a notification model (5.29 layout included) are skipped, and a freshly ejected config/notifications.ts then imports the 5.29 model path. In an app that already has src/app/notifications, no second model or migration is added, existing files are kept (and listed), and notFound is merged into an existing utils/locales.json. The mark-read controller turns a numeric :id into a number (integer ids on the default MongoDB stack) and keeps other ids as strings; the list query drops unknown keys such as a cache-busting _ instead of rejecting them.

Image derivatives are cached per source (<cacheDirectory>/<2 hex>/<sourceKey>/<size-mtime>/<hash>.<ext>). Deleting or moving a file through a local disk (delete, deleteMany, move, and deleteDirectory for every file under it) removes its derivatives, and a rewritten source's old derivatives are pruned once a new one is written, so the cache no longer grows forever. Pruning re-checks the source first, so a request that read an older version never deletes the newer version's derivatives, and a derivative pruned mid-request is rendered again instead of answering 500.
Concurrent variant requests for the same file on two disks (a mirror copied with its mtime) no longer share one generation, which left the second target unwritten and answered 500.

A warning is logged once when the image-variant cache sits inside the public folder: a configured uploads.images.cacheDirectory is shared by every local disk, so private derivatives there would be publicly served.

storage.use(name) (and StorageManagerContract.use) is typed as ScopedStorage, the class it returns, so deleteDirectory, copyDirectory, moveDirectory, emptyDirectory, putFromUrl, prepend and append type-check without a cast.
middleware.rateLimit() returns an async middleware (its in-memory path still completes synchronously).

The run-app skill lists where each pnpm version reads build approvals (allowBuilds on 10.26+, workspace onlyBuiltDependencies on 10.5–10.25, package.json before 10.5); it used to say only allowBuilds works.

Graceful shutdown no longer waits out its timeout on keep-alive connections whose request finished during the drain: in-flight responses answer Connection: close and connections are closed as they go idle (default forceCloseConnections: "idle"), so later connectors still shut down. Active responses are never cut short.

A response.sse() or response.stream() started after graceful shutdown began keeps the drain's Connection: close; its own Connection: keep-alive used to override it and hold close() until the shutdown timeout.

response.sse() removes line breaks and NUL from event names and ids, and writes a multi-line comment() as one comment line per line, so values built from user input cannot inject SSE fields or events.
An onDisconnect handler on response.sse() or response.stream() that throws is logged and no longer crashes the process or skips the handlers after it.

warlock.config.ts loads when it imports local TypeScript without an extension (./src/connectors/local) or through a tsconfig paths alias, on Node without native TypeScript and with native type stripping alike. The fallback bundles the config's local graph with esbuild, keeps packages external (one BaseConnector/container identity), runs the config once, rethrows its own errors unchanged, keeps each inlined module's import.meta.url, and removes its temp file.
v.file() rule methods (maxSize, image, accept, mimeType, …) return this, so the UploadedFile output type survives the chain; saveTo() is typed as a string output.

The dev server and the HTTP test server register module src/app/<module>/utils/locales.json dictionaries at boot; they were left out of the boot file set, so t() printed raw keys until the file was edited.
The HTTP test server no longer keeps Vitest's main process alive after teardown: the loader-hook MessagePort is unreferenced except while a version-bump flush waits for its acknowledgement.

A quoted config key ("machine-thumb", 'single-quoted') is written to .warlock/typings/config.d.ts without its quotes, so the generated file stays valid TypeScript; computed keys are skipped, and a quoted storage driver name is no longer quoted twice. The typings manifest now records its generator version, and a manifest written by an older version is discarded, so a config.d.ts broken by 5.29 is regenerated on the first boot after upgrading instead of only when a config file changes.

The circular-dependency check no longer reports a file as importing itself because a comment mentions import("./same-file"): the regex fallback ignores comments and self imports are not dependency edges. Comments are found with the TypeScript parser, so a regex literal such as /\/*$/ or // inside JSX text is never mistaken for one and the imports after it are kept. A pure export type { X } from re-export adds no dependency edge on either parsing path.
warlock add web's src/web/root.tsx stub notes that <Head /> renders the viewport tag (metadata.viewport changes or disables it) and does not hand-write a second one.
Mail logs no longer print recipient addresses: send, development, test-mode, partial-rejection and error lines show m***@example.com. MailResult and a thrown MailError still carry the real addresses.
http.rateLimit had no way to share counts between processes except an ioredis client, which the node-redis connection of @warlock.js/cache cannot provide.

Request log snapshots mask credential query parameters (code, signature, sig, X-Amz-*, X-Goog-*, the logger's secret keys and http.logging.redactQueryParams) in the parsed query too, not only in url; OAuth authorization codes no longer reach log lines. New redactQueryCredentials().
warlock.config.ts fallback: a catch-all tsconfig paths pattern ("*": ["./types/*"]) no longer inlines packages into the config bundle; an alias is inlined only when it resolves outside node_modules.

warlock.config.ts fallback: import.meta.url/dirname/filename are replaced only where they are real expressions, so the same words inside a string or comment no longer break or alter the bundled config.

warlock.config.ts fallback runs only for the config's own unresolved relative or aliased imports (not for a package that is not installed, or a module missing inside node_modules), and also when native type stripping refuses the TypeScript (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX, ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING). A loading error in the bundled config names warlock.config.ts instead of the temporary module.

warlock add image on pnpm 9 and 10.0–10.4 no longer creates a settings-only pnpm-workspace.yaml (packages field missing or empty): the sharp approval goes where the installed pnpm reads it (package.json pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies before 10.5, the workspace's onlyBuiltDependencies on 10.5–10.25, allowBuilds from 10.26). Inside a parent pnpm workspace no per-app file is written.
<Form query={{ … }}> sets the query string of the URL the form posts to (the current page, or to's page), without touching the body or the named action.

<Form independent> submits alongside a pending submission instead of sharing it: a Cancel next to a long-running Start. Neither aborts the other; a double submit of the same form with the same fields still shares one request, another form posting the same action (a Cancel per row) never does, and unmounting a form cancels only its own submission. Its result, redirect included, is dropped once the user has moved to another page.
LinkPropsWithout<K> and DistributiveOmit<T, K>: omit props from LinkProps without collapsing its destination union, so a wrapper keeps the required-params check.
isRouteName(name) narrows a data-driven string to a route name after checking the published route table, so it reaches <Link to> or href() without a cast.

metadata.viewport (string | false). <Head /> now emits <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> by default, so a new app lays out at device width on phones; a meta entry named viewport is still honoured. Like the charset it is document-level: client navigation never rewrites it, nor a viewport tag root.tsx writes itself.
webConnector({ build: { testOnly } }): app-root-relative folders or files the production build's page-graph scan skips.

A page action that redirects now ends its submission once the redirected page is on screen: useIsSubmitting() stays true and onSuccess waits until the destination's fresh loader data has committed, so a revision-guarded form cannot resubmit stale data.
useIsSubmitting() is true while any submission is in flight, including independent ones.

A production start no longer loads Vite, Rollup or @babel/parser: the web connector imports its Vite dev-server config, page-registry plugin, dev route installer, dev 404 reporter and the sitemap's page-walk fallback only on the development path, so its static graph shrinks from 185 to 67 modules.

<Form> honours the submit button's formAction and its name/value. The enhanced path posted to the form's URL; with no navigation runtime the fallback called form.submit(), which dropped both. Without a runtime the browser now submits natively, and a late fallback re-submits through the same button.

A page request the client abandoned before its loaders finished no longer renders: it stops with ClientDisconnectedError before anything is committed, and the page handler neither reports it nor writes a response. It used to render layouts without their loader data and log a 500. A loader timeout on a connected request still renders its 504.

A 4xx error page (a thrown ForbiddenError/BadRequestError, a failed page validation) now hydrates. The client payload gate accepted only 500–599 and only name/message/stack, so it refused the 4xx status, the validation errors and the production errorCode the server sends, and logged "hydration payload … could not be read".
The production build's import.meta.url / static-asset scan skips *.spec.* and *.test.* files and __tests__ / __mocks__ folders; a test helper under src/web no longer fails warlock build.

Web's React contexts (locale, document, session) live in one Symbol.for registry on globalThis, so a second evaluation of their module under warlock dev reuses them instead of making useLocale() throw "called outside Warlock's LocaleProvider" until restart.
A request abandoned between the layout and page loaders no longer renders the page with data undefined; covered by the abandoned-request fix above, with a regression test for this case.
An abandoned page request still reports a genuine failure (a loader or session-resolver bug) that happened before the disconnect; only failures the abort itself caused stay silent.

An independent submission no longer draws the page the user left over the page a navigation already in flight committed, and a page swap no longer leaves another operation's pending commit unresolved, which could keep useIsNavigating() true and hang a redirect's wait.
The build's test-folder skip reads folder names below the web root, so an app located under a __tests__ folder is still scanned.

A redirect target is followed or emitted only when it is relative or http:/https:. response.redirect() in a loader or action throws for javascript:, data: and other schemes (and for control characters), so redirect(request.input("next")) can no longer send script to the browser; the client refuses such an x-warlock-redirect header and never hands one to window.location.assign().

<Form> enhances only same-origin http(s) targets. A submit button whose formaction names another origin is posted natively instead of being fetched, so the page never trusts another origin's redirect header or page payload.
TypedValidationResult<T> and ValidatedOutput<T> types.

pnpm bench:types measures inference compile cost on a generated composed-schema project (16 entities, 8 services) and fails when instantiations or types grow more than 5% over bench/types-baseline.json. It also fails when it cannot read a metric or is given a malformed option, warns when the TypeScript version differs from the baseline's (--strict makes that a failure), and removes its temporary project on Ctrl+C.
validate() takes data: unknown instead of any.
Infer.Input/Infer.Output of an object is one flat object type instead of an intersection of its optional and required halves; the shape is unchanged and compile cost moves by 0.1%.
pnpm typecheck now also checks the expectTypeOf assertions in tests/unit/types/ (tsconfig.typecheck.json); they were never enforced before.
.refine() callbacks stay value: any on purpose: custom rules run before an object or array validates its children, so the value is not the schema output.

Behaviour change: v.union([...]) now checks a present empty value ("") against its members instead of accepting it unchecked; a missing key is still the required/.optional() question. v.union([v.literal("x"), v.int()]).present() now rejects "".
validate() keeps the typed output of v.record(...) (Record<string, …>); only an index signature over any/unknown (the wide Schema) stays any.

v.literal("") accepts a present "" again (regressed in 5.25): its default (implicit) required state and .present() keep it, .optional() and .nullable() no longer drop it. An explicit .required() or requiredIf(...) still rejects "". A literal set without a blank value still reads "" as missing.

A field with an empty default (v.string().max(n).default("")) no longer fails "is required" when the input omits it, sends null, or sends a blank string (an untouched HTML input); the output is the default.

A null default no longer satisfies "required" on a field that is not .nullable(), and an empty default of the wrong type (v.int().default("")) now fails the type rule instead of being returned unchecked.

v.discriminatedUnion(...).optional() accepts an absent, undefined or null field, as every other validator does; .default(...) replaces null too and is validated through its branch. A required union reports a missing or null field with the required error; .nullable() keeps null.
schema["~standard"].validate(...) on a discriminated union resolves to the branch output union instead of unknown.

log.onChannelError(handler) / configure({ onChannelError }) and the ChannelErrorHandler type: receives a channel's sync throw or async rejection from log(), a redaction that threw, or a timed-out flush(). Default: one stderr line. The handler may be async; a rejection is swallowed.

maskEmail(address) and maskEmailsInText(text): mask email addresses (m***@example.com) inside message strings and cache keys, which key-based redaction cannot reach. Core's mail logs and the cache drivers' key logs use them.
Logging is fire-and-forget: level methods no longer return a promise, so @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises no longer flags every call site.

log.flush() drains every channel concurrently: each waits for its own in-flight async deliveries (including entries logged while the flush runs), then runs its flush(), so a hung network channel no longer holds up the file channel.

log.flush({ timeout }) is bounded: it resolves after timeout ms (default 5000, DEFAULT_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS; Infinity waits without a limit) and reports each channel still draining to the channel error handler. Before, one delivery that never settled made flush() (and a graceful shutdown awaiting it) wait forever.
maskEmailsInText cuts text longer than MASK_EMAILS_MAX_LENGTH (16,384 characters) and marks the cut, so masking a huge cache key or message has a bounded cost.

A channel whose log() rejected became an unhandled rejection (looping through captureAnyUnhandledRejection), and one that threw synchronously stopped delivery to the channels after it; both are now isolated and reported to the channel error handler.

A redaction that threw (a censor function that fails on an unexpected value) threw at the call site and skipped the remaining channels. A channel's own redaction failure is now isolated like any channel failure; a logger-wide one drops the entry (it is never delivered unredacted) and is reported to the channel error handler.
An async onChannelError handler that rejected became an unhandled rejection.

Security: maskEmailsInText backtracked quadratically on long runs of address-like characters with no domain (about 11 s on 75 KB), and it runs on cache keys built from request input. Its pattern is now bounded and linear. It also masks addresses with letters from any script (jöhn@exämple.de), and maskEmail no longer keeps half of a surrogate pair.

Provider content blocks: ProviderContentBlock ({ provider, type, data }) on ModelResponse.blocks, the streaming done chunk, Message.blocks, CapturedMessage.blocks, LLMTrip.blocks and AgentResult.blocks. The agent copies a response's blocks onto the assistant turn so the adapter can replay it verbatim (thinking, compaction).
FinishReason values context_exceeded, pause_turn and refusal. The agent resumes a pause_turn by replaying the paused turn, within maxTrips.
toolDispatch: "concurrent" | "sequential" on AgentConfig and AgentExecuteOptions (ToolDispatchMode), concurrent by default.

maxConcurrentTools on AgentConfig and AgentExecuteOptions (default 4): the cap on a trip's tool calls running at once, so a model (or a prompt injected into its context) cannot start an unbounded number of tool calls in one turn.
mapWithConcurrency(items, limit, mapper) utility: an order-preserving Promise.all with a concurrency cap.
ModelCallOptions.providerOptions (adapter-only options keyed by wire format) and cacheControl.ttl ("5m" | "1h").
MockModelResponse.blocks for scripting provider blocks in tests.
The semantic cache no longer stores a paused (pause_turn) turn as a final answer, and stores a resumed turn whole (every segment), not only its last segment.

VCR request hashes include providerOptions, so two calls that differ only in provider options (betas, context_management, …) no longer replay the same recording. It joins the hash only when a provider entry carries a value — {}, { anthropic: {} } and { anthropic: { betas: undefined } } hash like no providerOptions — so existing cassettes recorded without it still match. cacheControl (breakpoints, ttl) stays out of the hash: it changes billing, not output.

Responses with thinking, redacted-thinking, compaction, server-tool or cited-text blocks return the whole ordered turn as ModelResponse.blocks (and on the streaming done chunk); an assistant message carrying Anthropic blocks is replayed verbatim.

providerOptions.anthropic (AnthropicCallOptions): betas routes the call through client.beta.messages, body merges extra request fields last (context_management, fallbacks, inference_geo, …), thinkingDisplay sets thinking.display.
AnthropicModel.countTokens(messages, options?) counts input tokens through messages.countTokens; AnthropicModel is exported and AnthropicSDK.model() returns it.
Per-call cacheControl.ttl overrides the model's promptCacheTtl.
Consecutive tool results are sent as one user message with several tool_result blocks, as Anthropic expects for parallel tool use.
Claude 5-family thinking rules: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5 / 5.1 never receive budget_tokens or disabled.

effort: "none" on Claude Sonnet 5.5 sends thinking: { type: "between_tools" } (its only thinking-off form, sent alone with no output_config.effort or display); it used to omit thinking, so the model still thought at its default effort. Opus 5.5 and Fable 5 / 5.1 have no thinking-off form and keep omitting thinking.
providerOptions.anthropic.thinkingDisplay is applied only to adaptive thinking, so it is never sent beside between_tools (a 400).

Security: a stored block is replayed only when its data.type equals its declared type and the type is one Claude returns on an assistant turn (text, thinking, redacted thinking, tool use, server-tool use and results, MCP, container upload, compaction). A transcript from outside the process can no longer smuggle a tool_use or user-side block past the tool-id check; such turns are rebuilt from content + toolCalls.

exec() takes a per-call signal (ExecOptions); run_shell and run_tests pass the agent run's ctx.signal. An already-aborted signal never starts the command; an abort mid-run kills the process tree. Both resolve with the new cancelled: true on RunShellResult, never together with timedOut.

WorkspaceBackendExecOptions.signal and WorkspaceBackendExecResult.cancelled? for custom backends; the local backend removes its abort listener when the command settles, and the mock backend honours a pre-aborted signal.
Read results carry startLine, endLine, truncated, bytesCapped and totalBytes; readFile() and the read_file tool now return the same ReadFileResult for the same arguments.

read.maxBytes is enforced: the returned content (line-number prefixes and newlines included) never exceeds it, so a single long line no longer bypasses the cap. Lines are cut on a character boundary, never mid-character; hash remains the SHA-256 of the whole file.
Command output clipped at shell.maxOutputBytes is cut on a character boundary instead of ending in a replacement character.
A read window past the end of the file returns empty content instead of one numbered empty line.

Writes, edits and removes of the same path are serialized, so two concurrent edit_file calls (the agent now dispatches a trip's tool calls concurrently) can no longer both pass the stale-hash guard and silently drop one edit; the second re-reads and is rejected as stale, or applies on top when it pinned no hash.
Aborting a command after it has already exited (while its stdio is still draining) no longer reports it as cancelled; the tree is still reaped so the result settles.
On Windows, a taskkill that cannot be started no longer crashes the process with an unhandled 'error' event; the direct child is killed instead.

Email addresses inside logged cache keys are masked (user.member@example.com logs as u***@example.com), in the base driver's operation log, in error lines (written even with logging off: SWR refresh failures, lock release, clone failures), in the "Cannot increment non-numeric value" error, and in the null driver.

redis driver increment() works on Redis 6. With a default ttl configured it ran EXPIRE … NX, which only Redis 7+ accepts: on Redis 6 the call threw after the count had already gone up, which silently disabled login throttles and the cache-backed rate limiter. The increment and the default TTL are now applied together by one Lua script, and a TTL the counter already has is never shortened.

The default increment() (file and null drivers) reads a counter's value and deadline in one read. A counter that expired between two separate reads used to be rewritten from its stale value with no expiry at all, and every increment rounded the remaining TTL up, pushing the deadline up to a second later each time.

file driver: an entry stored without a TTL (its expiresAt is written to JSON as null) was read back by the internal entry reader as already expired, so swr() freshness checks and TTL-preserving writes treated it as missing.
Selecting notifications scaffolds the smaller, convention-following src/app/notifications module that warlock add notifications now writes (see @warlock.js/core).

New apps get the viewport tag from <Head /> (@warlock.js/web 5.30.0), so phones lay pages out at device width and responsive CSS applies; the scaffolded src/web/root.tsx says so and does not hand-write a second one.

pnpm before 10.5 could not install a new app (ERROR packages field missing or empty): pnpm 7–9 and 10.0–10.4 reject the settings-only pnpm-workspace.yaml. The scaffold now reads pnpm --version and writes approvals where that version reads them: no workspace file and pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies in package.json before 10.5; the workspace file plus onlyBuiltDependencies on 10.5–10.25 (which ignore allowBuilds); the unchanged allowBuilds file on 10.26+, 11 and 12. It does not add packages: ["."], which fails every later pnpm add on those versions (ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT). Feature approvals (sharp) follow the same rule; apps inside an existing workspace still get neither.

The feature multiselect no longer prints stacked copies of itself in a short or narrow terminal: the 22-option list pages to the terminal's height, and each row's hint is shortened to fit one line (a wrapped row made clack redraw below the previous frame). The AI and agent-target multiselects use the same sizing. @clack/prompts is now ^0.8.2, the first version whose multiselect pages.

The login throttle keys accounts and IPs by a keyed hash (auth.throttle.count.email.<hmac>, auth.throttle.count.ip.<hmac>) instead of the raw address or IP, so cache logs never show them. The HMAC key is derived from auth.accessToken.secret (as the OTP code MAC is), so a list of known addresses cannot reverse it; without a configured secret it falls back to SHA-256. The value is trimmed and lower-cased first, so " Sara@x.io" and "sara@x.io" share one bucket. Applies to loginThrottleMiddleware and every preset built on it (token issue/consume, OTP); a custom identify is used as is. throttleIdentifierHash(kind, value) is exported.

A throttle lock stores its own deadline, so a cache driver with sliding expiration (memoryExtended) can no longer keep a retrying client locked past lockoutDuration. Locks written by 5.29 (true) are still honoured until they expire.
The throttle warns once when the cache driver is null, which stores nothing, so the throttle can never lock.

moveDirectoryNoReplaceAsync(from, to, { expectedSource?, syncParents? }) (also fs.dirs.moveNoReplace): moves a directory only when nothing holds the destination, refusing atomically instead of replacing an empty directory the way rename() does. It claims the name with an exclusive mkdir, renames over that placeholder, verifies the moved (dev, ino) and never falls back to copy + delete.

DirectoryMoveError with outcome (not-moved: this call moved and replaced nothing / moved / uncertain), reason, and placeholderCleanupError when the empty placeholder it claimed could not be removed; directoryIdentityAsync() and the DirectoryIdentity type. When the source vanishes just before the rename the claim is released and the error is not-moved / source-identity-mismatch. The destination parent may be a symlink to a directory (macOS /tmp, a deploy current link). POSIX only: refuses explicitly on Windows and across filesystems.
Docs and skills point at the model path warlock add notifications writes since 5.30.0: app/notifications/models/notification/notification.model.

releases.summaryHtml: Fixes for applications upgrading from 5.27, typed nullable and list resources, and one module graph in dev. locales.json files under $sites/<site>/… (and other $ folders) work again: the folder only names the group when $group is missing (a 5.27 regression). In warlock dev, the dev server has its own Vite cache so a vitest run no longer breaks it, multi-site roots get their site's translations, the original error of a broken page is logged first instead of a follow-on useLocale() error, and src/app modules imported by pages share the instance the API side uses. New in @warlock.js/core: nullable(Resource) for resources that may be null (resources, responseSchema, OpenAPI, route types) and [Resource] list fields in defineResource; cast strings inside arrayOf item schemas are no longer dropped. useTrans() returns string instead of any. Every package's skills now refer to other topics by name, so the links work after they are copied into an app. Lockstep release across all 31 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.29.0 tarballs passed install, typecheck, a fresh migrate and seed, devtools in dev with the API docs, a production build with browser smoke, and the --role=worker and --role=api starts; after publishing, the same check passed against npm.

items.html: warlock dev uses its own Vite cache (node_modules/.vite/warlock-dev), so a vitest run that re-optimizes dependencies no longer wipes the dev server's cache and 500s every SSR page until a restart.

The original error is no longer hidden behind a follow-on one. When a client navigation cannot build the page tree (e.g. a server-only barrel imported from browser code), the original error is kept across the forced reload and logged first as the ROOT CAUSE; later errors in that document, such as "useLocale() was called outside Warlock's LocaleProvider", are marked as probable consequences. On the server, a page module that fails to load logs its original error at install time, and an error page that itself fails is reported as a consequence naming the root cause. onClientError receives the new "navigation" kind.

useTrans() returns a typed translator: it returns string, not any, and keys are still checked against TranslationKeyRegistry. Translate is one plain signature, so a lambda passed where a Translate is expected (label((key) => t(key))) keeps its parameter type. New type exports: TranslateFor, TranslationConverter, InlineTranslation.

Multi-site apps in warlock dev: a site's root.tsx and its locales.json are keyed by the same site folder (as in production), so the root LocaleProvider gets the site dictionary instead of {}, including when the client rebuilds after an SSR failure.

locales.json files under $-prefixed folders (src/web/$sites/<site>/..., guard folders) no longer fail warlock generate.typings, dev or build with "segments must match …" (5.27 regression). The folder-derived namespace is computed only when the file declares no $group, and skips $ folders and the site name after $sites.

warlock dev: an src/app module imported by a page, layout or root is the same instance the API side uses (one module graph), so module state such as an AsyncLocalStorage set in middleware, caches and registries is shared between controllers and page loaders. Pages reach those modules through a trampoline to the native module core already loaded. Modules that (transitively) import @warlock.js/web, live in src/web, are client-bound, or need Vite (import.meta.env/glob/hot, CSS or asset imports) keep loading through Vite as before. Dev only; production builds are unchanged.

nullable(Resource): a resource that may be null, accepted as a defineResource field and in responseSchema bodies. A field outputs null (not omitted) for null/undefined input; ResourceOutput/ResponseBodyOutput type it as Output | null; OpenAPI documents it as oneOf [resource, null]; route types emit … | null.

[Resource] list fields in defineResource: each item is mapped through the resource, [] stays [], and the output type is an array (the same syntax responseSchema already accepts). Plain Resource fields behave as before.

Cast strings inside an arrayOf({...}) item schema ("number", "string?", "date", "string[]") were silently dropped from the resource output; they are now cast like top-level fields, matching the output type.
parseLocaleDictionary() accepts defaultNamespace as a function, called only when the file declares no $group, so a folder that cannot name a namespace never fails a file with an explicit $group.

warlock dev publishes each src/app file it reloads ({ url, generation }, after the loader hook confirms the bump) through the development.appModules container key, so @warlock.js/web can load the same module instance in page loaders.

releases.summaryHtml: Postman collections, Swagger UI, and fixes from production use. warlock generate.postman writes a Postman Collection v2.1.0 from the same OpenAPI document as generate.openapi (tag folders, example bodies, saved responses, {{baseUrl}}/{{token}}, bearer auth on guarded routes), and @warlock.js/devtools adds Swagger UI beside Scalar at /__warlock/docs/swagger with OpenAPI and Postman downloads. The web skills were audited against the code and expanded (page metadata, cookies, images, testing pages, hydration debugging), and every package's llms.txt now lists each skill with its description. Fixed: replacing or unsetting a nested object in Cascade no longer leaves empty parent objects; expected 4xx errors log one warn line instead of an error-level stack; v.object() output follows the declared key order; the per-site sitemap is served as application/xml; an empty nested-resource list outputs []. Behaviour changes: set("field", obj) writes the nested object as one value; 4xx errors log at warn. Lockstep release across all 31 packages. Generator matrix scope: none; before publishing, the blog on the 5.28.0 tarballs passed install, typecheck, a fresh migrate and seed, devtools in dev including the API docs (OpenAPI, Postman, Scalar, Swagger UI), a production build with browser smoke, and the --role=worker and --role=api starts; after publishing, the same check passed against npm.

items.html: warlock generate.postman writes a Postman Collection v2.1.0 (storage/postman/collection.json, or --out) derived from the same OpenAPI document as generate.openapi (options: --title, --server, --include-pages), so the two can never disagree. Each tag is a folder, each operation a request with an example body generated from its schema (JSON as raw, multipart as form-data), saved responses for every declared status, {{baseUrl}} and {{token}} collection variables, collection-level bearer auth for authMiddleware() routes and noauth on public ones. openApiToPostmanCollection(document, options?) is exported (pure, deterministic _postman_id), and getDevelopmentPostmanCollection() returns the collection for the running dev process.

Expected client errors no longer fill logs with stack traces: a thrown error that resolves to a 4xx (an HttpError such as ConflictError or ResourceNotFoundError, or a DatabaseWriterValidationError configured below 500 via http.modelValidationErrorStatus) is logged once at warn as Name: message (status), without the stack. 5xx and unknown errors are logged at error with the stack, as before.
A nested-resource field whose input is an empty list now outputs []; it used to drop the key. null/undefined still omit it.

Swagger UI. /__warlock/docs/swagger renders the same OpenAPI document with Swagger UI (Apache-2.0), and the dashboard's API tab has a Scalar | Swagger UI switch (Scalar stays the default; the choice is remembered in the browser). The prebuilt swagger-ui-dist 5.33.0 bundle and stylesheet are vendored in ui/vendor/swagger-ui/ with their license and notice and served as assets/swagger-ui-bundle.js and assets/swagger-ui.css, so apps install no extra dependencies. The schema validator badge is off, so the page makes no outside request.
Downloads in the API tab. OpenAPI JSON (/__warlock/api/openapi.json) and Postman collection links.

GET /__warlock/api/postman.json returns the Postman collection for the registered routes, built by core's getDevelopmentPostmanCollection(). It answers 503 when the host's core cannot build one, with the same dev-only, loopback-only guard.

Replacing a nested object on MongoDB (model.set("nested", obj).save()) now writes the whole new object with one $set, instead of diffing per leaf. Removing keys no longer leaves their parents behind as empty {} objects in the stored document. Dotted-path sets (set("nested.a", v)) and merge() stay partial per-leaf updates, so concurrent writes to other keys still survive. SQL drivers already replace the whole JSON column and are unchanged.

unset("nested.x") now removes the parents it empties (unset("a.b.c") on { a: { b: { c: 1 } } } stores no a), and the update $unsets that parent rather than leaving {}. A parent is pruned only when that unset emptied it: an object stored or set as {} is left alone, and arrays are never pruned. unset("nested") removes the whole object.
Multi-site apps: the per-site sitemap is served as application/xml; it was text/plain (the handler set the XML header, then response.text() overwrote it).
New apps: a failed AI-skills sync during install now prints a warning with the fix (the skills:sync script) instead of a silent skills-sync-skipped.
New apps: AGENTS.md describes the app as full-stack (APIs plus src/web/** pages) and points agents to the warlock-js-web skill.
